column3: German artist (1939-2017); jazz musician; Born in Dresden; Citizenship: Germany.
Danish jazz drummer Aage Tanggaard recorded with Warne Marsh and Kenny Drew in 1980 and with Svend Asmussen's quartet in 1999.
Bassist Aaron Bell anchored Duke Ellington's orchestra in 1960-62, including the 'Nutcracker Suite', then worked as an arranger and jazz educator.
Classical composer Aaron Copland wrote his 1948 Clarinet Concerto for jazz clarinetist Benny Goodman. Its second movement uses jazz idioms and a clarinet smear.
Jazz pianist Aaron Goldberg's trio with Reuben Rogers and Eric Harland made 'Worlds' (2006), featuring guests Luciana Souza and Kurt Rosenwinkel.
Pianist Aaron Parks recorded 'Find the Way' with bassist Ben Street and drummer Billy Hart in October 2015; ECM released the lyrical trio set in 2017.
Clarinetist Aaron Sachs formed the Manor Re-Bops in 1946 and recorded Clarinet and Co. in 1957 with Jimmy Raney, Hall Overton and Osie Johnson.
Jazz drummer Aaron Scott was part of McCoy Tyner trio with bassist Avery Sharpe and played on Tyner album Infinity with Michael Brecker in 1995.
Free-jazz cellist Abdul Wadud recorded the solo album 'By Myself' (1977); his cello also shaped Julius Hemphill's 'Dogon A.D.' (1972).
South African pianist (1934-2026) mixed jazz and Cape rhythms. 'Mannenberg' (1974) became an anti-apartheid anthem; worked with Duke Ellington; played Mandela's 1994 inauguration.
American bandleader, songwriter; jazz musician; Member of Abe Lyman's California Orchestra; 1897-1957; Instruments: drum kit; Born in Chicago; Citizenship: United States.
Swing clarinetist Abe Most joined Les Brown in 1939 and played with Tommy Dorsey in 1946 before becoming a busy Los Angeles studio musician.
New Orleans-raised trumpeter Abram Wilson blended jazz, blues and storytelling. His final Philippa project traced the life of pianist Philippa Schuyler.
American guitarist; born Fred Leroy Robinson (1939-2009); Recorded on: Acid Truth; Member of The Night Blooming Jazzmen; Co-recorded with Bob Magnusson; Born in Memphis.
American jazz pianist (1910-1964); Recorded on: After Hours; Co-recorded with Andy Penn; Instruments: piano; Born in New York City; Citizenship: United States.
Pianist Achim Kaufmann co-led 'Pith & Twig' (2014) with bassist Robert Landfermann and drummer Christian Lillinger in the experimental trio gruenen.
Israeli singer and political activist; born 1969; Instruments: guitar, percussion instrument, piano; Born in Tel Aviv.
Dutch flugelhorn player Ack van Rooyen co-founded the United Jazz + Rock Ensemble and played in Gil Evans's and Peter Herbolzheimer's orchestras.
British clarinetist Acker Bilk formed the Bristol Paramount Jazz Band. His instrumental Stranger on the Shore became the United Kingdom's biggest-selling single of 1962.
German musician and conductor (1900-1971); Born in Berlin; Citizenship: Germany.
Keyboardist Adam Holzman performed with Miles Davis in 1985-89, serving as musical director during Davis's late electric-jazz period.
German musician; Recorded on: Ammi all schangi; Co-recorded with Florian Schneider; born 1967; Instruments: trumpet, jazz violin; Citizenship: Germany.
Jazz vocalist whose wordless style shaped early swing. Recorded 'Creole Love Call' and 'The Blues I Love to Sing' with Duke Ellington's orchestra in October 1927.
Jazz harpist Adele Girard recorded with Joe Marsala's ensemble in 1944 and appeared on two Barbara Lea performances at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in 1957.
Japanese pianist and vocalist Akiko Yano made her solo debut with Japanese Girl in 1976 and later collaborated with Yellow Magic Orchestra and the duo yanokami.
Guitarist Al Di Meola joined Chick Corea's Return to Forever in 1974, recording 'Romantic Warrior' (1976) before a solo jazz-fusion career including 'Elegant Gypsy'.
Soul/gospel singer Al Green released 'Back Up Train' with the Soul Mates in 1967 (R&B hit in 1968); later shaped Hi Records' Memphis sound with Willie Mitchell.
Bebop pianist Al Haig recorded with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker in the 1940s and joined Miles Davis's early 'Birth of the Cool' sessions.
Vocalist Al Jarreau won the 1982 Grammy for jazz vocal Blue Rondo a la Turk and also won pop vocal honors for Breakin Away.
American entertainer, actor, and singer (1886-1950); Recorded on: Alexander's Ragtime Band; Co-recorded with Bing Crosby; Instruments: voice; Citizenship: Russian Empire.
Jazz trumpeter Al Killian recorded with Earle Spencer's progressive big band in Hollywood in September and October 1946.
Bassist Al Lucas recorded Boneology and Down Vernon's Alley with J.J. Johnson, Leo Parker, Hank Jones and Shadow Wilson for Savoy in New York on Dec. 24, 1947.
Tenor saxophonist Al Sears joined Duke Ellington's orchestra in 1944, played on its 1945 It Don't Mean a Thing remake and recorded Swingville leader albums in 1960.
British artist (1920-2014); jazz musician; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Grangemouth; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Alan Greenspan played in Henry Jerome's New York swing band (1944-45), long before his career as Federal Reserve chairman.
American computer scientist (born 1940); jazz musician; Born in Springfield; Citizenship: United States.
British saxophonist Alan Wakeman worked with Paul Lytton and Harry Miller before performing with Mike Westbrook, Graham Collier and Soft Machine.
Tenor saxophonist whose raw timbre, marching-song motifs and intense improvisations made him a distinctive free-jazz voice.
Blues/jazz singer (1895-1984), Harlem Renaissance star. Recorded 'How Long, Sweet Daddy, How Long?' (1921); sang with King Oliver at Chicago's Dreamland Cafe; toured Europe 1927.
Venezuelan arranger Aldemaro Romero helped create the Onda Nueva style, combining joropo with contemporary popular and jazz influences.
Soviet Jazz composer, pianist, arranger and conductor (1906-1971); Instruments: piano, violin; Born in Zaporizhzhia; Citizenship: Soviet Union.
Cypriot vocalist Alexia Vassiliou spans jazz, experimental music and Greek popular song, using improvisation and conceptual projects.
Saxophonist Pee Wee Ellis arranged and co-wrote James Brown's 'Cold Sweat' and 'Licking Stick', bringing jazz horns into the foundations of funk.
Swedish singer Alice Babs was a featured soloist in Duke Ellington's Second Sacred Concert in New York in 1968 and Third Sacred Concert in London in 1973.
Pianist, harpist and composer whose spiritual-jazz recordings combine modal improvisation with strings, organ and meditative textures.
French clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Alix Combelle recorded 'Crazy Rhythm' in Paris in August 1935 with the Quintette du Hot Club de France.
British fusion guitarist Allan Holdsworth issued I.O.U. in 1982 and recorded Road Games with bassist Jeff Berlin and drummer Chad Wackerman in 1983.
New Orleans pianist, songwriter, arranger and producer Allen Toussaint released Southern Nights and performed his songs at Joe's Pub in New York in 2009.
Fusion drummer Alphonse Mouzon played on Weather Report's debut and became a member of Larry Coryell's Eleventh House in the mid-1970s.
Trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire's 2020 Blue Note quartet album 'on the tender spot of every calloused moment' reimagines the blues with Sam Harris and Harish Raghavan.
London singer Amy Winehouse debuted with jazz-influenced Frank in 2003 and released Back to Black in 2006; Rehab won 2008 Grammy Song and Record of the Year.
Israeli-born jazz clarinetist Anat Cohen blends swing with Brazilian choro; 'Rosa Dos Ventos' pairs her with Trio Brasileiro on choro-inspired music.
Romanian vocalist Anca Parghel recorded the Klaus Ignatzek Trio album Airballoon in the Netherlands in March and April 1992.
Norwegian pianist Anders Aarum debuted his trio on Lucky Strike in 2000 and recorded Oslo Puzzle with Jens Fossum and Hermund Nygard in 2023.
Norwegian pianist Andreas Ulvo made Eple Trio's debut 'Made This' (2007) with bassist Sigurd Hole and drummer Jonas Sjovaag, drawing on Scandinavian jazz.
Pianist and composer whose idiosyncratic post-bop harmony and open forms are heard on Point of Departure.
Jazz pianist Andy LaVerne studied with Bill Evans, toured with Stan Getz and recorded Four Miles with Randy Brecker, George Mraz and Al Foster.
Steelpan jazz musician Andy Narell released his first leader album in 1979 and developed calypso-inspired improvisation and music for large steel bands.
Guitarist Andy Summers released the 1989 solo album The Golden Wire with jazz players Paul McCandless and Jimmy Haslip.
Brazilian percussionist; jazz musician; Recorded on: Aguas-Iguais; Co-recorded with Davide Petrocca; born 1965; Born in Belo Horizonte.
Saxophonist Angelika Niescier led 'The Berlin Concert' (2017) with Christopher Tordini on bass and Tyshawn Sorey on drums; Intakt issued it in 2018.
French gypsy-jazz guitarist Angelo Debarre recorded Gypsy Guitars with guitarist Serge Camps and bassist Frank Anastasio, issued by Hot Club Records in 1989.
Jazz-influenced soul vocalist Anita Baker released The Songstress in 1983 and her Elektra breakthrough Rapture in 1986, featuring Sweet Love.
Singer Anita O'Day worked with Gene Krupa and Stan Kenton, then made influential Verve albums; her 1958 Newport performance became a jazz-film highlight.
British jazz vocalist Anita Wardell trained in Australia and at London's Guildhall School. Her early albums Why Do You Cry? and Straight Ahead feature jazz pianists.
German pianist Anke Helfrich recorded We'll Rise with Dietmar Fuhr, Jens Duppe and guest trombonist Adrian Mears, portraying pioneering women through jazz.
Dutch singer Ann Burton recorded Blue Burton in 1967 with Louis van Dijk, Jacques Schols, John Engels and Piet Noordijk; Artone issued it first.
American jazz singer and musician; born 1964; Instruments: voice, saxophone; Born in Belle Plaine; Citizenship: United States.
Composer Ann Ronell wrote Willow Weep for Me in 1932, dedicating the song to George Gershwin; her score is held in Duke Ellington archives.
German singer-songwriter Anna Depenbusch pairs poetic chanson writing with piano-led performances, including live analog direct-to-vinyl recording.
French drummer Anne Paceo composed 'Bright Shadows' (2019), joining Christophe Panzani's saxophone, Pierre Perchaud's guitar and Tony Paeleman's keys.
Dutch trombonist Annemarie Roelofs explored microtonal improvisation with ten-string guitarist Pascal Marzan on Berlin & London, issued in 2026.
German clarinetist Annette Maye combines jazz, world music and improvisation in ensembles including FisFuez and Vinograd Express.
Jazz vocalist Annie Ross recorded 'Twisted' in 1952, setting her own words to Wardell Gray's saxophone solo; she later joined Lambert, Hendricks & Ross.
British trombonist Annie Whitehead began with Ivy Benson's all-woman orchestra, later played jazz with Working Week and led her own 1984 album 'Mix Up'.
Cuban pianist and arranger Anselmo Sacasas co-founded Casino de la Playa in 1937 and later recorded his own orchestra's dance music for Victor.
American bandleader (1896-1969); jazz musician; Born in Oakland; Citizenship: United States.
Composer and saxophonist Anthony Braxton recorded solo works in the late 1960s and developed Creative Orchestra Music and the Ghost Trance Music system.
Keyboard improviser Anthony Coleman led Sephardic Tinge on three Tzadik albums (1995-2002), exploring Jewish musical traditions in downtown jazz.
Bassist Anthony Cox recorded That N This as solo acoustic bass in 2002. He also recorded Work with Steve Lacy and Daniel Humair and performed with Dave King's Vector Families.
Pianist-composer Anthony Davis built the flexible Episteme ensemble around composed and improvised music, later carrying its players into opera.
Contrabass guitarist Anthony Jackson recorded Voice, Move and Spark with pianist Hiromi and drummer Simon Phillips in the Trio Project.
Alto saxophonist Anthony Ortega recorded Jazz for Young Moderns in 1956, playing saxophones, clarinet and flute in separate Nat Pierce and Bob Zieff ensembles.
Australian composer, pianist and electronic musician whose experimental output spans orchestral commissions, improvised ensembles and electronic work.
Jazz guitarist Anthony Wilson accompanied Diana Krall at Paris's Olympia on Nov. 29-Dec. 2, 2001, on Live in Paris, issued by Verve in 2002.
Saxophonist Antoine Roney studied with Jackie McLean and played with Clifford Jordan, Donald Byrd and Elvin Jones. His trio also featured his son Kojo.
Finnish bassist and composer Antti Hytti worked with Edward Vesala and Tomasz Stanko, later leading free jazz projects and composing for film.
Polish-Greek guitarist Apostolis Anthimos played in SBB and led recordings such as Days We Can't Forget, while also joining Tomasz Stanko sessions.
Tenor saxophonist Archie Shepp recorded 'Attica Blues' in 1972, using large-ensemble soul and gospel colors to address the Attica prison uprising.
Chicago saxophonist Ari Brown joined the AACM in 1971 and led his Delmark debut 'Ultimate Frontier' in 1995, linking spiritual and avant-garde jazz.
Drummer Ari Hoenig led the 2008 album 'Bert's Playground'; his Punk Bop group was joined by Chris Potter and guitarist Jonathan Kreisberg.
Driving drummer and leader of the Jazz Messengers, a hard-bop school for generations of improvisers. His press-roll accents and ensemble energy are unmistakable.
West Coast alto saxophonist whose lyrical yet urgent playing mixes cool-jazz clarity with bebop and blues inflection.
Pianist famed for exceptional virtuosity, harmonic substitutions and dazzling reworkings of popular-song melodies.
Alto saxophonist Arthur Blythe's 'Lenox Avenue Breakdown' (1979) mixes free jazz and funk with tuba, flute and guitar; the septet includes James Blood Ulmer.
Clarinetist (1910-2004) led a swing orchestra that recorded 'Begin the Beguine' in 1938; his band briefly featured Billie Holiday, and he later performed at Carnegie Hall.
Cuban trumpeter Arturo Sandoval, mentored by Dizzy Gillespie, combines Afro-Cuban jazz phrasing and virtuoso trumpet playing with classical repertoire.
Osaka Hammond B-3 organist Atsuko Hashimoto recorded Time After Time with Yutaka Hashimoto and Jeff Hamilton and played US jazz dates in 1999.
Hungarian jazz guitarist Attila Zoller recorded Gypsy Cry with Herbie Hancock in 1969 and a final 1998 trio session with Tommy Flanagan and George Mraz.
Los Angeles pianist Austin Peralta combined jazz improvisation with electronics on his Brainfeeder album Endless Planets, working with saxophone and rhythm players.
Hamburg-born boogie-woogie pianist Axel Zwingenberger began recording in 1976 and recorded with Big Joe Turner in Los Angeles in May 1978.
Azerbaijani pianist and singer Aziza Mustafa Zadeh recorded Always in 1993 with John Patitucci and Dave Weckl and Dance of Fire in 1995.
Brazilian guitarist and vocalist Badi Assad recorded 'Solo' (1994) for Chesky; her percussive guitar and voice cross Brazilian music, classical technique and jazz.
British singer Barb Jungr recorded the Bob Dylan interpretation album Every Grain of Sand in 2002 and followed it with Just Like a Woman - Hymn to Nina in 2008.
German musician Barbara Buchholz brought the theremin into interdisciplinary performance after studying with Lydia Kavina in Moscow.
German musician; Recorded on: Apple & Egg; born 1957; Instruments: guitar, voice; Born in Kaiserslautern; Citizenship: Germany.
British saxophonist and composer Barbara Thompson led Paraphernalia, recorded with Jon Hiseman and issued jazz-rock recordings spanning BBC sessions and live concerts.
Singer Barbra Streisand's debut Columbia album appeared in 1963, arranged and conducted by Peter Matz. It included Gershwin and Fats Waller songs and won Album of the Year.
Australian pianist Barney McAll co-founded Groove Collective after moving to New York in the 1990s and released the leader albums Mooroolbark and Hearing the Blood.
Double bassist Barre Phillips recorded 'End To End' (2018), a solo ECM album of spontaneous acoustic improvisations informed by decades of free jazz.
Drummer Barrett Deems played in Louis Armstrong's band in the 1950s and appears on 'Satch Plays Fats' and 'Louis Armstrong Plays W. C. Handy'.
Brazilian bossa nova singer Bebel Gilberto blended acoustic bossa and electronica on the 2000 Ziriguiboom album Tanto Tempo, produced by Suba.
Mexican composer (1944-2003); Recorded on: El Galleton; Co-recorded with Chali Hernandez; Instruments: piano; Born in Quilmes; Citizenship: Mexico.
American entrepreneur, jazz tenor saxophonist, and bandleader; Recorded on: 3 O'Clock Blues; Co-recorded with B.B. King; 1924-1987; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Memphis.
Guitarist Ben Monder's ECM album 'Amorphae' pairs atmospheric guitar with drummers Paul Motian and Andrew Cyrille in open, textural improvisation.
Drummer Ben Riley played in Thelonious Monk's quartet in 1964-67 and later worked with Alice Coltrane, Ron Carter and the Monk-focused group Sphere.
Norwegian saxophonist Bendik Hofseth plays on Oystein Sevag's Caravan, recorded in Germany and Oslo during 2004 and 2005.
Trumpeter Benny Bailey played with Gillespie's and Hampton's big bands; his Candid LP 'Big Brass' (1960 session) features Phil Woods and Julius Watkins.
Tenor saxophonist/composer (1929-2024) wrote 'I Remember Clifford' and 'Killer Joe'; played with Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers and founded the Jazztet with Art Farmer.
Clarinetist and bandleader central to the swing era; led celebrated big bands and small groups and played at Carnegie Hall in 1938.
column4: The Famous 1938 Carnegie Hall Jazz Concert

column3: German drummer Benny Greb leads the Benny Greb Brass Band, blending jazz and funk, and also records with Moving Parts. His releases include Brassband.
British jazz saxophonist and writer (1927-1998); Recorded on: Caravan; Co-recorded with Count Basie; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Leeds; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Swing trombonist Benny Morton played with Fletcher Henderson in the late 1920s and joined Count Basie in 1937, remaining until 1940.
Trombonist Benny Powell played the bridge on Count Basie's hit 'April in Paris'; his bold tenor and bass trombone sound connected swing to bebop.
French multi-instrumentalist Bernard Lubat shaped the Uzeste jazz scene through his Compagnie Lubat and festival work.
Dutch trombonist Bert Boeren recorded live in The Hague on June 21, 2024 with Four Others and previously played in the Dutch Swing College Band from 1985 to 1999.
American classic blues, jazz, and cabaret singer; 1895-1955; Instruments: voice; Born in Cleveland; Citizenship: United States.
Jazz harpist Betty Glamann worked with Spike Jones and led a quintet with bassist Rufus Smith. Duke Ellington brought her into his orchestra after hearing her in 1955.
American musician (1899-1964); Recorded on: A Shanty in Old Shanty Town; Member of Andre Ekyan et son orchestre; Instruments: clarinet, saxophone, voice; Citizenship: United States
Tuba player Bill Barber performed with Miles Davis's nonet on the 1949-50 Birth of the Cool recordings and later appeared on Miles Ahead and Porgy and Bess.
Drummer Bill Bruford led the jazz-rock band Bruford on 'Feels Good to Me' (1978), with guitarist Allan Holdsworth and keyboardist Dave Stewart.
Trumpeter Bill Chase led the brass-heavy jazz-rock band Chase. Their hit 'Get It On' (1971) featured a four-trumpet section plus organ, guitar, bass and drums.
Bassist Bill Crow joined Gerry Mulligan's sextet in 1954, playing with Zoot Sims and Bob Brookmeyer in a long association with Mulligan.
Jazz organist and pianist Bill Doggett recorded with Paul Quinichette in 1951, Illinois Jacquet in 1946 and led Columbia organ-combo sessions.
Pianist who brought luminous voicings and close bass-drum interaction to the jazz trio. Hear the Village Vanguard recordings and Waltz for Debby.
Bassist/producer Bill Laswell's Material project released 'Hallucination Engine' (1994), mixing jazz improvisation, dub grooves and Indian music.
Hawaiian jazz ukulele pioneer Bill Tapia played swing guitar for decades and returned to recording the ukulele on Tropical Swing and Duke of Uke.
Singer whose flexible timing and intimate tone made familiar melodies sound deeply personal. Lady in Satin and earlier small-group sides show different eras.
Jazz guitarist Billy Bauer played on Lennie Tristano's 1949 'Intuition' session with Lee Konitz and Warne Marsh, opening space for collective improvisation.
Fusion drummer Billy Cobham propelled Mahavishnu Orchestra, then led 'Spectrum' (1973), merging intricate jazz rhythms with rock, funk and Jan Hammer's keyboards.
Singer and bandleader Billy Eckstine formed a groundbreaking bebop big band in 1944, with Dizzy Gillespie as music director and Charlie Parker leading the saxes.
Drummer Billy Hart recorded ECM's 'All Our Reasons' (2012) with Ethan Iverson, Mark Turner and Ben Street, balancing rhythmic swing and abstraction.
Drummer Billy Higgins brought supple swing to Ornette Coleman's 1959 quartet; his sensitive drumming later supported countless hard-bop Blue Note sessions.
British guitarist, composer and bandleader associated with adventurous improvisation, blues and jazz, and founder of the Voice of God Collective.
Singer Bing Crosby was one of Paul Whiteman's Rhythm Boys singing on the Feb. 18, 1928 Victor 21274 recording of Mississippi Mud with the jazz-age orchestra.
Cornetist (1903-1931) famed for lyrical early-jazz solos. Hear 'Singin' the Blues' (1927), recorded in New York with Frankie Trumbauer's orchestra.
Bandleader Blanche Calloway launched the Joy Boys in 1931; her touring orchestra and swing recordings broke barriers for Black women directing bands.
Mississippi-born pianist Blind John Davis worked on Chicago blues sessions for Lester Melrose in 1937-42 with Tampa Red, Big Bill Broonzy and Memphis Minnie.
New Orleans blues singer Blue Lu Barker recorded Don't You Feel My Leg in 1938, worked alongside guitarist Danny Barker and made a final live recording at Jazz Fest in 1998.
Tenor saxophonist Bob Berg played in Miles Davis's electric band in 1984-86 after work with Horace Silver, Chick Corea and Cedar Walton.
New Orleans drummer Bob French led the Original Tuxedo Jazz Band after his father in 1977 and recorded Marsalis Music Honors Bob French in 2007.
Baritone saxophonist Bob Gordon recorded 'Meet Mr. Gordon' in Los Angeles in May 1954 with arranger Jack Montrose, a West Coast chamber-jazz session.
Saxophonist Bob Mintzer toured with Jaco Pastorius's Word of Mouth band in 1981-82. He founded a New York big band in 1983 and joined Yellowjackets in 1990.
Jazz alto saxophonist Bob Mover played in the Charles Mingus Jazz Workshop and with Chet Baker, then recorded the 1978 Vanguard album Sweet Basil.
Flautist Bobbi Humphrey made the 1973 Blue Note crossover album Blacks and Blues with Larry and Fonce Mizell's jazz-funk production.
American singer and songwriter whose career crossed early rock and roll, swing interpretations of standards, folk and country music.
Cornetist Bobby Hackett's lyrical solo on Glenn Miller's 'A String of Pearls' (recorded 1941) gave the swing hit a delicate New Orleans-jazz color.
American pianist and keyboardist Bobby Lyle debuted as a leader with the Wayne Henderson-produced 1977 fusion LP The Genie, later recording Ivory Dreams.
Vocal improviser Bobby McFerrin recorded the all-voice album Simple Pleasures in 1988. He founded Voicestra and made Circlesongs from spontaneous choral music.
Hard-bop pianist and composer whose gospel-rooted grooves helped shape the sound of Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers.
Brazilian guitarist Bola Sete recorded Mambossa with Vince Guaraldi, Fred Marshall and Jerry Granelli in 1963 and played on Guaraldi's Live at El Matador.
French trumpeter and author Boris Vian joined Hot Club de France in 1937, played with Claude Abadie's jazz band, and helped animate Paris's Tabou club in 1947.
Bandleader Boyd Raeburn led a racially mixed, bebop-oriented big band from 1942 to 1949 with musicians including Roy Eldridge, Dizzy Gillespie and Oscar Pettiford.
Pianist whose trio playing combines contrapuntal clarity, shifting meters and reinterpretations of rock and pop repertoire.
Los Angeles trombonist Britt Woodman worked with Les Hite and Boyd Raeburn before joining Duke Ellington, who featured him on the Such Sweet Thunder suite.
Pianist Bross Townsend worked with Charles Mingus and Milt Jackson and accompanied singers Dinah Washington and Dakota Staton.
Jazz pianist Bruce Barth worked with Stanley Turrentine and Terence Blanchard after moving to New York in 1988; his trio recorded live at the Village Vanguard.
Jazz drummer Bruce Ditmas led the 1995 Postcards album What If with John Abercrombie, Paul Bley, Dominic Richards and Sam Rivers; he wrote its title track.
Jazz guitarist Bruce Forman leads the western-bebop band Cow Bop and recorded soundtrack performances for three Clint Eastwood films, including Million Dollar Baby.
English musician (1922-1993); Recorded on: A Child Is Born; Instruments: clarinet, saxophone; Born in Saltburn-by-the-Sea; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
American ragtime composer (1884-1952); Instruments: piano; Born in Oberlin; Citizenship: United States.
Swiss saxophonist Bruno Spoerri began electronic experiments in 1965 and co-founded the Swiss Society for Computer Music in 1982.
Italian bassist Bruno Tommaso recorded Blues Waltz in Rome in October 1990 with pianist Gianni Lenoci and drummer Antonio Di Lorenzo.
British drummer Bryan Spring played drums, percussion and timpani on Nucleus jazz-fusion album Under the Sun, originally issued by Vertigo in 1974.
Norwegian oboist Brynjar Hoff worked in major orchestras and also played jazz with Karin Krog, moving between chamber music and improvisation.
American musician; 1922-2002; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Fayetteville; Citizenship: United States.
Trumpeter Buck Clayton joined Count Basie in 1936; his solo on 'Fiesta in Blue' and arrangements such as 'Taps Miller' shaped classic swing.
Washington tenor saxophonist Buck Hill recorded Capital Hill at Van Gelder Studio in 1989 with pianist Barry Harris, bassist Ray Drummond and drummer Freddie Waits.
American guitarist; born 1969; Instruments: guitar, electric bass guitar, mandolin; Born in Huntington Beach; Citizenship: United States.
Guitarist Bucky Pizzarelli performed in The Tonight Show band during the 1960s and 1970s, toured with Benny Goodman and recorded with veteran swing players including Zoot Sims.
Pianist whose fleet single-note right-hand lines and modern left-hand comping helped establish the language of bebop piano.
Jazz banjoist Bud Scott recorded with King Oliver's Creole Jazz Band and Jimmie Noone's Apex Club Orchestra during early Chicago jazz.
Tenor saxophonist Budd Johnson worked with Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines in the 1930s and helped organize early bebop sessions in New York.
American jazz cornetist (1890-1931); Member of Camelia Brass Band; Instruments: trumpet; Born in White Castle; Citizenship: United States.
American jazz saxophonist; Recorded on: Aphrodisia; Co-recorded with Allan Beutler; 1926-2003; Instruments: saxophone; Born in The Bronx; Citizenship: United States.
Jazz bassist Buddy Banks recorded with Guy Lafitte in Paris in June 1954 and led his own Jazz de Chambre quartet with guitarist Jimmy Gourley.
Arranger and conductor Buddy Bregman orchestrated The Pajama Game, including its Bob Fosse dance sequences, and composed or arranged television scores.
Jazz bassist Buddy Catlett accompanied Johnny Griffin and Eddie Lockjaw Davis on Pisces and appears among the players on Goin' to the Meetin'.
Trumpeter Buddy Childers joined Stan Kenton's big band as lead trumpet in 1942 at just 16, later playing and writing for other major jazz orchestras.
Drummer Buddy Deppenschmidt played in Charlie Byrd's jazz trio with bassist Keter Betts on Blues Sonata and the 1960 Guitar Artistry sessions.
English jazz saxophonist (1909-1976); Recorded on: Accent on Swing; Co-recorded with Andy McDevitt; Instruments: saxophone; Born in 16th arrondissement of Paris.
Jazz singer and pianist Buddy Greco worked with Benny Goodman and recorded the live Buddy Greco at Mister Kelly's with bassist John Frigo in 1955.
American musician (1924-2000); Born in Hope; Citizenship: United States.
Trombonist Buddy Morrow played with Artie Shaw and Tommy Dorsey before leading an RCA Victor orchestra. He also directed the Glenn Miller Orchestra in 1974-75.
American musician; Recorded on: A Tender Word Will Mend It All; Co-recorded with Gene Krupa; 1922-1950; Instruments: voice; Born in Derry; Citizenship: United States.
American bassist Buell Neidlinger moved between Cecil Taylor's improvised jazz and concert work, establishing K2B2 Records with Marty Krystall.
Milwaukee alto saxophonist Bunky Green played in Charles Mingus's band and developed an adventurous modern jazz language over a long career.
Berlin percussionist Burkhard Beins joined Polwechsel in 2004; the quartet's Traces of Wood features member-composed pieces and electroacoustic improvisation.
Jazz pianist Burt Bales worked with the Yerba Buena Jazz Band and was recorded on Kansas City Stomp; his own recordings survive in the Stanford archive.
Pianist Burton Greene formed the Free Form Improvisation Ensemble with Alan Silva in 1963 and joined the Jazz Composers Guild the next year.
Free-jazz bassist Buschi Niebergall played on Globe Unity Orchestra's 'Live in Wuppertal', recorded March 25, 1973, with Evan Parker and Peter Kowald.
Trombonist Buster Cooper played with Lionel Hampton and in the Apollo Theater house band before serving in Duke Ellington's orchestra from 1962 to 1969.
Kansas City alto saxophonist Buster Smith mentored Charlie Parker and co-led a Band of Rhythm with Count Basie, shaping the Texas sax sound.
Bassist Buster Williams played in Herbie Hancock's Mwandishi sextet, appearing on 'Mwandishi' (1971), 'Crossings' (1972) and 'Sextant' (1973).
Swing drummer Butch Ballard toured Europe with Duke Ellington in 1950, played with Count Basie and worked with Cootie Williams at Harlem's Savoy Ballroom.
Drummer Butch Miles played in Count Basie's orchestra in 1975-79 and 1997-2007, carrying the forceful swing pulse of big-band jazz.
Cornetist Butch Morris devised 'Conduction', directing large improvising ensembles through gestures rather than fixed written scores.
Bassist Butch Warren played with Kenny Dorham at the Five Spot and worked on Blue Note sessions by Dexter Gordon, Herbie Hancock and others. He joined Thelonious Monk's quartet.
Drummer Buzzy Drootin toured with Jess Stacy by 1940, worked at Eddie Condon's New York club in 1947-51, and later formed a Boston jazz band.
Singer and bandleader Cab Calloway recorded 'Minnie the Moocher' (1931); its dramatic vocal performance entered the US National Recording Registry in 2018.
Jazz Musician, composer, entertainer (1921-2000); Recorded on: I Cried for You; Co-recorded with Eddie Taylor; Instruments: piano, voice; Born in London.
Afro-Cuban bassist Cachao and brother Orestes helped create mambo in 1937; he brought jazz-style jam sessions into Cuban dance music in 1957.
Jazz guitarist Cal Collins recorded on Scott Hamilton 2 for Concord Jazz in 1978 and performed alongside Herb Ellis, Ray Brown and Jake Hanna on Interplay.
Trumpeter-composer Cal Massey wrote Bakai for John Coltrane and Cry of My People for Archie Shepp; his compositions were also recorded by Lee Morgan and Jackie McLean.
American musician (1911-1971); Recorded on: A Man Is Like a Tree; Co-recorded with Albert Ayler; Instruments: piano, organ; Born in Springfield; Citizenship: United States.
Guitarist Calvin Newborn recorded Atlantic's Here Is Phineas on May 3, 1956 with pianist Phineas Newborn Jr., bassist Oscar Pettiford and drummer Kenny Clarke.
Bassist Cameron Brown recorded Here and How! in Brussels in November 1997 with Dave Ballou, Leon Parker, Sheila Jordan and guest Dewey Redman.
American actor (1913-1999); jazz musician; Recorded on: Let's Begin; Co-recorded with Fred Astaire; Born in New Orleans; Citizenship: United States.
Dutch saxophonist Candy Dulfer began leading a band at 13; her 1990 solo debut Saxuality received a Grammy nomination.
Alto saxophonist with a rich blues-inflected sound who bridged hard bop, soul jazz and modal playing; heard with Miles Davis and his own quintet.
Trombonist Carl Fontana's solo on Stan Kenton's 'Intermission Riff' showed a nimble, expressive trombone voice; he also played with Woody Herman.
Swing guitarist Carl Kress developed an elaborate chordal acoustic style, played with Paul Whiteman in 1926 and recorded guitar duets with Eddie Lang.
Norwegian bassist Carl Morten Iversen recorded Trio '87 with pianist Armen Donelian and drummer Audun Kleive in Oslo on July 11, 1987; all three co-wrote Song With No Name.
Trumpeter Carl Saunders worked with Stan Kenton in 1961-62, joined Bill Holman's Los Angeles orchestra in 1984 and led Bebop Big Band on Sea Breeze.
Composer and bandleader (1936-2023) shaped avant-garde jazz with 'Escalator over the Hill'; worked with Michael Mantler and Charlie Haden and toured Europe and Japan.
Detroit-born vocalist Carla Cook combines jazz swing with gospel and Motown influences. Her debut It's All About Love earned a Grammy nomination, followed by Dem Bones.
Electric bassist Carles Benavent joined Paco de Lucia's sextet in 1981 and worked with Chick Corea on 'Touchstone' (1982), connecting jazz and flamenco.
Jazz vocalist and bassist Carline Ray sang and played guitar with the International Sweethearts of Rhythm and released Vocal Sides in 2013.
British drummer Carlo Krahmer led a January 11, 1948 London Esquire session with Humphrey Lyttelton and Wally Fawkes, recording That Da Da Strain.
Italian percussionist Carlo Rizzo mixes jazz with early music. The French national library credits him with a polytimbral tambourine invention and membership in Tambour Quartet.
Portuguese flutist Carlos Bechegas recorded Open Secrets with Peter Kowald in 2001 and Secrets Under Trees with Ernesto and Guilherme Rodrigues in 2023.
Portuguese bassist and composer Carlos Bica formed Azul with guitarist Frank Mobus and drummer Jim Black. Their 1996 album blended lyrical jazz and rock textures.
Argentinian jazz musician and guitarist; born 1964; Citizenship: Argentina.
German pianist and songwriter (1931-2000); Recorded on: Autobahn; Member of C-jam All Stars; Co-recorded with Clark Terry; Instruments: piano; Born in Buenos Aires.
Panamanian-American musician; Recorded on: A Night in Tunisia; Co-recorded with Art Blakey; 1938-2023; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Panama Canal Zone.
Brazilian bossa nova composer Carlos Lyra introduced Primavera to Paul Winter after the 1962 Carnegie Hall concert; Winter later recorded the song.
American record producer and jazz pianist; born 1978; Instruments: piano; Born in Detroit; Citizenship: United States.
Panama-born alto saxophonist and flutist Carlos Ward played on Don Cherry's Relativity Suite and worked with Abdullah Ibrahim and Cecil Taylor.
Portuguese violinist Carlos Zingaro recorded the improvising trio Trizmaris in Lisbon in March 2023 with bassist Joao Madeira and drummer Sofia Borges.
Trumpeter Carmell Jones played on Horace Silver's 'Song for My Father' (1964) with Joe Henderson, Teddy Smith and Roger Humphries before moving to Berlin.
Canadian vocalist and composer (1903-1971); Recorded on: A Nightingale Sang in Berkeley Square; Instruments: saxophone, voice; Born in London; Citizenship: Canada.
Jazz vocalist-composer Carmen Lundy debuted with 'Good Morning Kiss' (1985) and recorded 'Modern Ancestors' (2019) and 'Fade to Black' (2022).
Rhythm guitarist Carmen Mastren worked with Tommy Dorsey in 1936-40 and recorded with Sidney Bechet and Muggsy Spanier in 1940, later joining Glenn Miller's Army band.
Singer/pianist (1920-1994) brought subtle phrasing to jazz ballads. Sang with Benny Carter and Count Basie; recorded 'Carmen Sings Monk' (1988) and played Montreux.
Caro Emerald is a Dutch pop-jazz recording project fronted by Caroline van der Leeuw, combining vintage big-band and Latin sounds with sampled beats.
Canadian jazz vocalist and pianist Carol Welsman performs multilingual standards and Latin jazz; her 2020 Dance with Me project features Juan Luis Guerra.
Munich jazz saxophonist Carolyn Breuer recorded A Family Affair with her father Hermann for Enja in 1993 and released Acquaintance in 1997.
American singer; 1925-2012; Born in Fort Gaines; Citizenship: United States.
Chicago jazz violinist-bandleader Carroll Dickerson led Sunset Cafe orchestras joined by Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines in the 1920s.
Bassist Carson Smith joined the pianoless Gerry Mulligan quartet with Chet Baker in 1952, later playing in small groups led by Russ Freeman and Chico Hamilton.
Berlin pianist Carsten Daerr led the Carsten Daerr Trio, whose 2007 Insomniac Wonderworld and 2010 Wide Angle mixed modern jazz with rock energy.
Danish pianist Carsten Dahl recorded Painting Music in 2019 with bassist Nils Bo Davidsen and drummer Stefan Pasborg, releasing the trio project on ACT.
American musician and singer; Recorded on: All About That Bass (2015 European cast); Co-recorded with Adam Kubota; born 1991; Instruments: voice; Born in Austin.
Harpist Casper Reardon trained under Carlos Salzedo and played with the Philadelphia Orchestra. He later explored jazz with Bunny Berigan and recorded on Jack Teagarden's Junk Man.
Chicago pianist Cassino Simpson recorded Tea for Two and It Dont Mean a Thing at Elgin in May 1942; one side appeared on SD in 1947.
Clarinetist and tenor saxophonist Castor McCord recorded Dinah and Tiger Rag with Louis Armstrong's orchestra for OKeh in New York on May 4, 1930.
Trumpeter Cat Anderson joined Duke Ellington in 1944, left to lead a band in 1947-49, and was noted for precise, brilliant high-register solos.
Swing vocalist Catherine Russell recorded Send For Me with guitarist-director Matt Munisteri, bassist Tal Ronen and drummer Mark McLean for Dot Time in 2022.
Trumpeter Cecil Bridgewater recorded Max Roach's In the Light in Milan on July 22-23, 1982, in a quartet with Odean Pope and Calvin Hill.
American jazz drummer Cecil Brooks III led the 1989 Muse album The Collective with Greg Osby, Gary Thomas, Geri Allen and Lonnie Plaxico.
Bassist Cecil McBee led 'Mutima' (recorded May 1974), bringing African-influenced rhythms and searching modal improvisation to Strata-East jazz.
Clarinetist and saxophonist Cecil Scott played on Teddy Wilson's February 18, 1937 New York Brunswick session backing Billie Holiday on The Mood That I'm In.
Pianist Cedar Walton wrote 'Mosaic' and 'Ugetsu' for Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers, then co-founded Eastern Rebellion with Clifford Jordan in 1974.
American musician (1914-1969); Recorded on: Ain't Misbehavin'; Co-recorded with Alton Redd; Instruments: piano; Born in Houston; Citizenship: United States.
Dutch jazz drummer Cees See played on 1958 Jacobs Brothers sessions, including the Fontana recordings Four and other Hilversum dates.
Brazilian guitarist and songwriter Celso Fonseca collaborated on albums with lyricist Ronaldo Bastos and recorded Pagina Central with Marcos Valle in 2009.
Drummer Chad Wackerman toured and recorded with Frank Zappa for seven years and worked extensively with guitarist Allan Holdsworth, including eight albums.
Singer Chaka Khan performed jazz standards on 'Echoes of an Era' (1982) with Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Chick Corea, Stanley Clarke and Lenny White.
Jazz pianist and singer Champian Fulton recorded Meet Me at Birdland live in September 2022 with Hide Tanaka and Fukushi Tainaka.
American blues pianist (1910-1992); Instruments: piano, voice; Born in New Orleans; Citizenship: United States.
Cuban conga player (1915-1948) joined Dizzy Gillespie; they performed at Carnegie Hall in 1947 and recorded 'Manteca', bringing Afro-Cuban rhythms into modern jazz.
St. Louis drummer Charles Bobo Shaw co-founded the Black Artists Group and led the Human Arts Ensemble, joining free jazz energy to funk rhythms.
Australian jazz flautist; born 1946; Instruments: flute; Born in Sydney.
French author, jazz expert (1911-1988); Born in 6th arrondissement of Paris; Citizenship: France.
Cuban bassist Charles Flores recorded Michel Camilo's Live at the Blue Note with drummer Horacio Hernandez during March 2003.
American musician (1927-1993); Recorded on: 52nd Street Theme; Co-recorded with Archie Shepp; Instruments: trombone; Born in Detroit; Citizenship: United States.
Organist Charles Kynard combined soul jazz with electric bass playing; he recorded Where It's At for Pacific Jazz in 1963 and Afro-Disiac for Prestige in 1970.
Belgian pianist Charles Loos co-founded the Loos-Lazarevitch International Quintet and recorded with Eric Legnini, Steve Houben and Maurane.
Alto saxophonist Charles McPherson recorded 'Bebop Revisited!' with pianist Barry Harris and trumpeter Carmell Jones on November 20, 1964.
Bassist, composer and bandleader whose works blend blues, gospel, counterpoint and collective improvisation. His groups often balance tightly written music with raw freedom.
Drummer Charles Moffett played in Ornette Coleman's trio with David Izenzon during 1965-67 and recorded with Archie Shepp on Four for Trane.
New Orleans saxophonist Charles Neville played in the Dew Drop Inn house band, joined the Neville Brothers and lent saxophone to Yellow Moon.
Trumpeter Charles Tolliver and pianist Stanley Cowell founded Strata-East in 1971 after recording the Music Inc. big band, championing artist-owned jazz.
Baritone saxophonist Charles Tyler worked with Albert Ayler on Bells and Spirits Rejoice before making free-jazz leader dates for ESP-Disk.
Pianist and jazz educator Charlie Banacos taught Mike Stern and Danilo Perez; his Pelaghia was premiered at Carnegie Recital Hall in 1984.
Saxophonist Charlie Barnet led an orchestra filmed performing Skyliner, Andy's Boogie and Cherokee. Smithsonian reels document his tenor, soprano and alto playing.
Canadian musician (1926-2003); Instruments: double bass; Born in Philadelphia; Citizenship: United States.
American actor, comedian, and jazz drummer (1927-2011); Recorded on: Boo Bop Bopbop Bop (I Love You, Too); Co-recorded with Sean Marshall; Born in Brooklyn.
American musician; Member of Harvey Lankford Synco Hi-Hatters; 1890-1951; Instruments: saxophone, trumpet, accordion; Born in Missouri; Citizenship: United States.
Banjoist Charlie Dixon recorded with Fletcher Henderson's orchestra on Copenhagen, Sugar Foot Stomp and other early New York jazz sides.
Baritone saxophonist Charlie Fowlkes joined Count Basie's band in 1953 after playing with Lionel Hampton, anchoring the saxophone section's low voice.
Bassist Charlie Haden (1937-2014) played on Ornette Coleman's 'The Shape of Jazz to Come' (1959); founded the Liberation Music Orchestra with Carla Bley in 1969.
Alto saxophonist Charlie Holmes joined Luis Russell in 1928; he later played in Louis Armstrong's backing band and with Cootie Williams.
Jazz-funk guitarist Charlie Hunter played bass lines and melodies at once on his custom eight-string guitar; hear the 1995 trio album 'Bing, Bing, Bing!'.
Pianist and bandleader Charlie Johnson recorded New York Harlem jazz in 1927-1929. A French national-library catalogue credits his piano and orchestra direction.
Solo pianist of popular music, recording artist (1896-1958); Recorded on: I'm in a Dancing Mood; Member of Charlie Kunz & The Casani Club Orchestra; Co-recorded with George Barclay
Alto saxophonist whose fluid, harmonically daring lines helped define bebop. His improvisations recast the blues and the changes of popular songs.
Tenor saxophonist Charlie Rouse brought a dry, melodic bop tone to Thelonious Monk's quartet from 1959-70; earlier he co-led the Jazz Modes.
Trumpeter Charlie Shavers arranged for John Kirby's agile swing sextet and co-wrote the jazz standard 'Undecided', first popular in 1939.
Trumpeter Charlie Teagarden recorded Beale Street Blues with Eddie Lang and Joe Venuti's All-Stars in 1931 and joined Paul Whiteman's band in 1933.
Tenor saxophonist Charlie Ventura played with Gene Krupa and founded 'Bop for the People' in 1946, taking accessible bebop arrangements to dance audiences.
Drummer Charlie Watts led a jazz quintet on 'A Tribute to Charlie Parker with Strings' (1992), featuring saxophonist Peter King and bassist Dave Green.
Swiss drummer Charly Antolini worked with Sidney Bechet and Albert Nicholas in Paris, then played with Benny Goodman, Earl Hines and Art Farmer.
Drummer Ches Smith led We All Break on 'Path of Seven Colors' (2021), combining Haitian Vodou drumming and jazz improvisation with pianist Matt Mitchell.
American drummer Chester Thompson bridged jazz fusion and rock, touring with Genesis and leading his own Nashville-based piano trio.
Guitarists Chet Atkins and Les Paul revisited jazz standards including 'Caravan' on their 1976 duet album 'Chester & Lester', crossing country and jazz guitar.
Trumpeter and vocalist associated with West Coast cool jazz; known for a lyrical, restrained tone and intimate singing as well as turbulent personal history.
Pianist and composer who explored acoustic trio jazz, Latin rhythms and electric fusion, including Return to Forever.
column4: Now He Sings, Now He Sobs

column3: Brazilian singer and songwriter Chico Buarque recorded hundreds of songs, often drawing on samba and theatrical writing across a long discography.
Tenor saxophonist Chico Freeman recorded 'Spirit Sensitive' (1978-79) with pianist John Hicks, bassist Cecil McBee and drummer Billy Hart.
Cuban composer Chico O'Farrill orchestrated Afro Cuban Jazz Suite in 1950 for an ensemble involving Machito, Charlie Parker and Buddy Rich.
Canadian musician; born 1972; Instruments: piano, voice; Born in Montreal; Citizenship: Canada.
Vocalist China Forbes joined Pink Martini in 1995 and co-wrote and sang Sympathique with pianist Thomas Lauderdale on their 1997 Heinz Records debut album.
Bongos player Chino Pozo recorded with Phineas Newborn Jr. on Jamaica in 1957 and performed percussion with Rene Bloch's 1962 Latin orchestra.
American musician; Recorded on: 'round Midnight; born 1950; Instruments: double bass, bass instrument; Born in Rockville Centre; Citizenship: United States.
Chromatic harmonica player Chris Bauer performs bop, ballads and Latin jazz standards. His album 'In A Yuletide Groove' interprets seasonal songs in a swing style.
German pianist; Recorded on: Aeolian Green; born 1953; Instruments: piano; Born in Trier; Citizenship: Germany.
British saxophonist and alto clarinetist Chris Biscoe played in Didier Levallet's Orchestre National de Jazz on Sequences, recorded in 1999.
Tenor saxophonist Chris Cheek recorded 'I Wish I Knew' in 1996-97 with guitarist Kurt Rosenwinkel, bassist Chris Higgins and drummer Jorge Rossy.
American jazz drummer (1902-2002); Instruments: drum kit; Born in Greenville; Citizenship: United States.
Swing guitarist Chris Flory recorded City Life for Concord in 1993 with John Bunch, John Webber and Chuck Riggs after years in Scott Hamilton's group.
German jazz pianist Chris Gall has led trio recordings on ACT and expanded into solo piano, orchestral projects and film composition.
Belgian percussionist Chris Joris recorded Until the Darkness Fades live in Mechelen with violin, cello and guest saxophone, blending improvisation and chamber music.
Saxophonist Chris Kelsey records experimental jazz and has led more than twenty projects across C.I.M.P., Unseen Rain and his own labels. He also wrote the novel Where the Hurt Is.
Bassist Chris Laurence played on Kenny Wheeler's Songs for Quintet, recorded at Abbey Road in December 2013 with Stan Sulzmann, John Parricelli and Martin France.
Pianist Chris McGregor led the multiracial South African Blue Notes and, in exile, Brotherhood of Breath, joining township rhythms to free jazz.
Jazz-rock fusion guitarist Chris Poland co-founded OHM with bassist Robertino Pagliari; their 2003 debut featured drummer David Eagle.
British trombonist Chris Pyne recorded John Surman's The Brass Project in London in April 1992 and appears on Kenny Wheeler's 1990 ECM large-ensemble album.
Bassist Chris White played on the 1967 New York sessions for Jimmy Owens and Kenny Barron's Atlantic quintet album You Had Better Listen, with Benny Maupin on reeds.
Memphis-born alto saxophonist Chris Woods first recorded as a leader for United in 1952, later played with Clark Terry and recorded Modus Operandi for Delmark in 1978.
R&B singer Chrisette Michele won a Grammy for Be OK with will.i.am in 2009 and received a Best R&B Album nomination for Better in 2014. Her debut I Am was issued in 2007.
Swedish actor and musician (1939-1986); Recorded on: Afro Temple; Co-recorded with Ali Lundbohm; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Bromma city district; Citizenship: Sweden.
French jazz pianist and arranger Christian Chevallier led 1950s small groups and orchestrated Kenny Clarke's 1957 Paris studio recordings.
French jazz drummer Christian Garros recorded with Roger Guerin, Christian Chevallier and Benny Golson in Paris sessions during 1956-1958.
Belgian trombonist Christian Kellens worked with Jack Sels and the Clarke-Boland orchestra, including international big-band recordings.
Drummer Christian Lillinger's 'Open Form for Society' (2019) linked chamber-like ensemble composition, dense rhythms, keyboards and free-jazz energy.
pianist; born 1974; Instruments: piano; Born in Kempten; Citizenship: Germany.
Austrian trombonist and composer Christian Muthspiel leads Orjazztra Vienna, whose albums include Homecoming (2022) and La Melodia della Strada (2023).
German pianist and music educator; born 1975; Instruments: piano; Citizenship: Germany.
Swiss double bassist Christian Weber explores improvisation, composed music and electronics, including projects with Wintsch and Wolfarth.
German reed player and composer Christina Fuchs co-leads FUCHSTHONE ORCHESTRA and records small-group work with accordionist Florian Stadler as FLUX.
Bassist Chubby Jackson played with Woody Herman and won the 1947 Down Beat bassist poll; he advocated a five-string upright bass for jazz.
American singer (1945-2021); Recorded on: Anthem for Old Souls; Co-recorded with Casey Waits; Instruments: voice; Born in Denver; Citizenship: United States.
American jazz pianist (born 1938); Recorded on: Blue Boy; Co-recorded with Al Cobbs; Instruments: piano; Born in Cambridge; Citizenship: United States.
American electric bassist and studio player whose rhythmically distinctive recordings span soul, rhythm and blues, pop and jazz fusion.
Canadian-Jamaican musician and beauty queen; born 1954; Born in Toronto; Citizenship: Canada.
Finland Swedish psychiatrist, author, musician and politician (1937-2019); Member of Scandia Jam Session; Instruments: piano; Born in Helsinki.
Jazz pianist and composer Clarence Williams accompanied Bessie Smith on her 1923 Columbia recording Gulf Coast Blues and led the early Blue Five.
British singer Cleo Laine combined jazz, classical repertoire and theater, gaining renown through John Dankworth's orchestra and concert stages.
Stride pianist Cliff Jackson recorded Horse Feathers and The Terror with his Krazy Kats in 1930 and later worked with Sidney Bechet in 1940-41.
Trumpeter whose clear articulation, lyrical phrasing and brilliant technique influenced hard bop despite his brief career.
Dutch composer, saxophonist and jazz musician (born 1941); Member of De Bumpers; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Amsterdam; Citizenship: Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Berlin jazz guitarist Coco Schumann joined the Ghetto Swingers in Theresienstadt in 1943, survived Auschwitz and continued performing jazz after the war.
Tenor saxophonist (1904-1969) helped establish the instrument in jazz. His celebrated 'Body and Soul' solo was recorded in New York in 1939 with Gene Rodgers and others.
British bassist and vocalist Colin Hodgkinson played in the trio Back Door with reed player Ron Aspery and drummer Tony Hicks, mixing blues and jazz.
Singer Connee Boswell sang lead in the Boswell Sisters, who recorded regularly from 1930 and appeared in The Big Broadcast in 1932; she continued solo after 1936.
German jazz trombonist (born 1943); Instruments: trombone; Born in Halle (Saale); Citizenship: Germany.
Dutch radio host and lawyer (1910-1992); jazz musician; Born in Crete; Citizenship: Kingdom of the Netherlands.
West Coast bop trumpeter Conte Candoli played with Woody Herman, Stan Kenton, Howard Rumsey and Shelly Manne, and joined Supersax in the 1970s.
British vocalist Corinne Bailey Rae moved from soulful pop into experimental music informed by artworks at Chicago's Stony Island Arts Bank.
Pianist and bandleader whose spare keyboard style, riff arrangements and buoyant rhythm section made Kansas City swing a defining sound.
American blues and jazz singer (1907-1989); Recorded on: Bad, Bad Baby Blues; Instruments: piano, voice, guitar; Born in St. John the Baptist Parish; Citizenship: United States.
Pittsburgh singer Dakota Staton signed with Capitol in 1954 and won DownBeat's newcomer honor in 1955; her 1957 debut album The Late, Late Show reached the pop charts.
Swiss drummer Daniel Humair played with Bud Powell and Chet Baker and formed a trio with Francois Jeanneau and Henri Texier. He was nominated for a Swiss music prize in 2015.
Bassist and producer Daniel Yvinec led the Orchestre National de Jazz as artistic director from 2009 to 2013. His programs addressed Robert Wyatt, Piazzolla and Billie Holiday.
Former tenor saxophonist Dannie Richmond switched to drums in 1955 and joined Charles Mingus; later he worked with Mingus Dynasty and the Adams-Pullen quartet.
French composer Darius Milhaud wrote La creation du monde in 1923, adapting jazz instrumentation after hearing Harlem jazz.
Pianist and bandleader whose quartet explored unusual meters and clear melodic contrasts; Time Out includes Paul Desmond's Take Five.
Singer-arranger Dave Lambert worked in Gene Krupa's orchestra in 1944-45 and recorded What's This? with Buddy Stewart in 1945.
American musician; Recorded on: Amanacer; 1932-2020; Instruments: piano; Born in Syracuse; Citizenship: United States.
Sydney-born trombonist Dave Panichi moved to New York in 1981 and played with the Buddy Rich Big Band. In 2017 he recorded a DVD of original big-band music called Paradigm.
Jazz guitarist Dave Stryker played with Stanley Turrentine and Jack McDuff; his 2024 Groove Street paired his organ trio with saxophonist Bob Mintzer.
Swing drummer Dave Tough joined the Woody Herman First Herd in 1944-45, helping shape its driving but understated swing-to-bop rhythm.
Cellist David Darling recorded Cycles at Talent Studio in Oslo in November 1981 with Collin Walcott, Steve Kuhn, Jan Garbarek, Arild Andersen and Oscar Castro-Neves.
Jazz guitarist David Gilmore recorded with Wayne Shorter on High Life and released leader albums including Numerology and Energies of Change.
American singer (born 1949); Recorded on: 3-Way Switch; Member of David Moss Dense Band; Instruments: voice; Born in New York City; Citizenship: United States.
Alto saxophonist David Sanborn debuted as a leader with Taking Off in 1975 and recorded Double Vision with Bob James in 1986.
American guitarist, composer and studio musician known for a gentle, recognizable soul-guitar touch and extensive work on popular and jazz recordings.
Guitarist David Torn mixed ambient textures and jazz-rock on 'Cloud About Mercury' (1987), recording with Mark Isham, Tony Levin and Bill Bruford.
American musician (1922-1957); Instruments: saxophone, trumpet; Born in California; Citizenship: United States.
American singer, actor, comedian and film producer (1917-1995); Recorded on: A Foggy Day in London Town; Member of Martin and Lewis; Instruments: voice; Born in Steubenville.
Vocalist Dee Dee Bridgewater's 'Red Earth: A Malian Journey' grew from 2006 Bamako sessions with Malian musicians, joining jazz voice to local traditions.
Singer Della Reese recorded pop and gospel music. Grammy nominations recognized her album Della and gospel recordings You Gave Me Love and Live! My Soul Feels Better Right Now.
French pianist and composer Denis Badault founded the thirteen-piece Bande a Badault and later directed the Orchestre National de Jazz.
Pianist Denman Fowler Maroney plays hyperpiano, combining keyboard action with prepared strings. His 2009 Udentity session featured Ned Rothenberg and Dave Ballou.
Bassist Dennis Irwin joined Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers in 1977 and later played almost every Monday with the Vanguard Jazz Orchestra.
British guitarist Derek Bailey's solo album 'Solo Guitar' (recorded 1971) reshaped free improvisation with fractured phrases and non-tonal guitar textures.
American jazz musician (1900-1994); Instruments: trumpet; Born in St. Louis; Citizenship: United States.
Tenor saxophonist with a broad tone and unhurried, behind-the-beat phrasing; a key bridge between swing and bebop.
Jazz singer-pianist Diana Krall recorded The Look of Love with Claus Ogerman's arrangements and the London Symphony Orchestra. Tommy LiPuma produced it.
American actor (1904-1963); jazz musician; Recorded on: By a Waterfall; Member of Charlie Davis and His Orchestra; Instruments: voice, piano; Born in Mountain View.
Pianist Dick Twardzik recorded a leader trio with Carson Smith and Peter Littman on October 27, 1954. He then joined Chet Baker's touring quartet in 1955.
Belgian pianist Diederik Wissels recorded the vocal chamber-jazz EP Sleepless with Ana Rocha and reed player Nicolas Kummert in November 2023.
Austrian pianist and conductor Dieter Glawischnig conducted the NDR Hannover orchestra for John Taylor's 1987 studio suite Quintessence.
Singer known as the Queen of the Blues who moved fluently among jazz, blues and rhythm-and-blues with clear diction and emotional control.
British singer; Recorded on: A Little Love; Played at Palais am Funkturm; born 1996; Instruments: guitar; Born in London Borough of Tower Hamlets; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Virtuoso trumpeter, composer and bandleader central to bebop and Afro-Cuban jazz; famed for angular lines, rhythmic play and work with Chano Pozo.
Belgian-born Romani guitarist whose dazzling improvisation and partnership with violinist Stephane Grappelli helped establish gypsy jazz.
Trumpeter Doc Cheatham backed blues singers in vaudeville during the 1920s, toured Europe with Sam Wooding and played lead trumpet with Cab Calloway in the 1930s.
Improvising vocalist Dominique Eade recorded two late-1990s RCA Victor jazz albums and has taught voice in New England Conservatory's jazz department.
Jazz pianist Don Abney played on Al Sears's Swing's the Thing, including his composition Ain't No Use, and on Lucy Reed's 1957 recordings.
Clarinetist Don Byron produced and arranged Bug Music, recorded at Master Sound in May 1996 with players including Kenny Davis, Uri Caine and Joey Baron.
American singer (1919-2004); Recorded on: Cuddle Up a Little Closer; Instruments: voice; Born in The Bronx; Citizenship: United States.
American musician (1923-1994); Recorded on: All the Things You Are; Instruments: trumpet; Born in Staten Island; Citizenship: United States.
British trombonist Don Lusher played leading big-band roles with Ted Heath and went on to lead ensembles and teach trombone.
Tenor saxophonist Don Wilkerson made three Blue Note leader albums with guitarist Grant Green after playing on Ray Charles sessions in the 1950s.
Jazz harpist Dorothy Ashby recorded The Jazz Harpist in 1957 and Hip Harp in 1958 with Frank Wess; her 1968 Afro-Harping expanded jazz harp into soul.
German singer-songwriter; born 1979; Instruments: voice; Born in Berlin; Citizenship: Germany.
British actor, comedian, composer and musician (1935-2002); Recorded on: Aftermyth of War; Member of Beyond the Fringe; Instruments: piano, organ; Born in Hammersmith.
German art historian and musician (1933-2018); Born in Remplin; Citizenship: Germany.
Composer, pianist and bandleader who wrote for the distinctive voices of his orchestra. His work spans intricate big-band portraits, suites and songs.
Duke Ellington's orchestra recorded Billy Strayhorn's 'Take the A Train' for Victor in February 1941; Ray Nance's trumpet solo became part of its identity.
Blues guitarist Duke Robillard co-founded Roomful of Blues with pianist Al Copley in Rhode Island in 1967 and later led his own swing- and jump-blues groups.
Alto saxophonist Earl Bostic had an R&B chart hit with 'Flamingo' (1951) on King Records; his 1952 band featured a young John Coltrane on tenor sax.
Acoustic guitarist Earl Klugh played on George Benson's White Rabbit and briefly joined Return to Forever. His 1979 duo album One on One paired him with Bob James.
Free-jazz drummer Ed Blackwell played with Ornette Coleman, Don Cherry and Charlie Haden on 1960 Atlantic sessions for 'This Is Our Music'.
Trumpeter Eddie Allen leads the jazz ensemble PUSH; his album The Rhythm features saxophonist Jonathan Beshay and guest trombonist Steve Turre.
Trombonist Eddie Bert played with Sam Donahue and Thelonious Monk, including Monk's 1959 ten-piece Town Hall ensemble.
Trumpeter Eddie Gale played on Cecil Taylor's Unit Structures and recorded the Blue Note leader albums Ghetto Music (1968) and Black Rhythm Happening (1969).
British pianist, music educator and jazz musician (1925-2012); Recorded on: Alligator Crawl; Member of Don Rendell Jazz Six; Instruments: piano; Born in Blackpool.
Vocalese singer Eddie Jefferson wrote lyrics to James Moody's improvised solo on I'm in the Mood for Love. King Pleasure recorded his adaptation in 1952.
American jazz and blues tenor saxophonist (1920-2010); Recorded on: A Spoonful of Sugar; Member of Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five; Instruments: saxophone.
Jazz guitarist Eddie Lang (1902-1933) recorded with blues guitarist Lonnie Johnson in New York in 1927 and 1929, helping establish jazz guitar as a solo voice.
American musician (1900-1955); Recorded on: A Porter's Love Song; Instruments: saxophone, clarinet; Citizenship: United States.
American electric blues guitarist and singer; Recorded on: A New Leaf; Member of The Eddie Taylor Blues Band; 1923-1985; Born in Benoit; Citizenship: United States.
Brazilian singer and composer Edu Lobo recorded Cantiga de Longe in Los Angeles in 1970 with Hermeto Pascoal and Airto Moreira among the guests.
Dutch jazz trumpeter, singer, arranger and composer; born 1978; Instruments: flugelhorn, trumpet, trombone; Born in Westerbork; Citizenship: Kingdom of the Netherlands.
German musician; 1894-1944; Instruments: jazz violin; Born in Kyiv; Citizenship: German Reich.
German saxophonist (1938-2017); Instruments: saxophone; Citizenship: Germany.
Brazilian pianist Eliane Elias recorded with Steps Ahead in 1983, then began her own bandleader career in 1986, linking Brazilian and jazz piano styles.
Norwegian jazz vocalist Elin Rosseland composed and sang the 2013 Trondheim Jazz Orchestra album Ekko, drawing on a large ensemble led by Erlend Skomsvoll.
Israeli female singer (1933-2010); Instruments: voice; Born in Tel Aviv.
Jazz vocalist celebrated for precise pitch, lively scat improvisations and wide-ranging Song Book recordings of American standards.
column4: Ella Fitzgerald Sings the Cole Porter Song Book

column3: Pianist Elliot Lawrence led the WCAU radio house band from 1945 and recorded with big bands for Columbia and Decca. He later conducted the Tony Awards broadcast.
Italian singer songwriter, composer, actor, stand-up comedian (1935-2013); Recorded on: "Grazie"; Member of I Cavalieri; Instruments: guitar, piano, voice; Born in Milan.
Tenor saxophonist Eric Alexander played in One for All on 'Live at Smoke Vol. 1' (2001) with Jim Rotondi and Steve Davis.
Blues guitarist Eric Clapton recorded the 2006 collaborative album The Road to Escondido with JJ Cale and earned a 2008 Grammy for it.
Adventurous improviser on alto saxophone, bass clarinet and flute whose angular phrases expanded jazz's sonic vocabulary.
Canadian acoustic guitarist Erik Mongrain writes contemporary fingerstyle compositions. His official site describes the eight-track album Tempo and his online guitar lessons.
