Pianist Mulgrew Miller joined Art Blakey Jazz Messengers in 1983, recorded his 1985 leader debut Keys to the City and played with Tony Williams.
Multi-reed jazz player Musa Kaleem recorded flute with Coleman Hawkins and Tiny Grimes in 1958 and tenor saxophone with Dizzy Reece in 1960.
Pianist Myra Melford's Fire and Water Quintet recorded 'For the Love of Fire and Water' (2022) with Mary Halvorson, Tomeka Reid and Susie Ibarra.
Jazz pianist Nadi Qamar, formerly Spaulding Givens, designed the Mama-Likembi instrument and recorded original music and instructional works for Folkways.
British vocalist Najma Akhtar blends Urdu ghazal with jazz phrasing and recorded crossover albums including Qareeb and Pukar.
Jazz vocalist and composer Nancy Harrow released Wild Women Don't Have the Blues on Candid and You Never Know on Atlantic, then wrote story-based jazz musicals.
Scat-focused jazz vocalist Nancy King made the 2006 duo album 'Live at Jazz Standard' with pianist Fred Hersch; she also worked with Glen Moore.
Saxophonist, flutist and singer Napoleon Murphy Brock joined Frank Zappa's band in 1973. He appears in the filmed Roxy shows and on recordings drawn from those performances.
Drummer Nasheet Waits recorded Baida at Avatar Studios in October 2012 with Ralph Alessi, Jason Moran and Drew Gress; ECM issued the album in 2013.
Pianist whose early trio style helped shape intimate small-combo jazz; later became a hugely successful singer of popular standards.
Trombonist Nat Peck entered Glenn Miller's wartime Army Air Force orchestra in 1944 and later performed in the Clarke-Boland Big Band.
Pianist-arranger Nat Pierce played with Woody Herman's Third Herd from 1951 to 1955, arranged the 1957 Sound of Jazz telecast and co-led the Capp-Pierce Juggernaut.
jazz musician; 1905-1963; Instruments: double bass; Born in New Orleans; Citizenship: United States.
Natalie Cole won the 1992 Grammy for Album of the Year with Unforgettable With Love. Her recording of Unforgettable with Nat King Cole won Record of the Year.
Guitarist Nate Radley joined pianist Kris Davis and the Infrasound octet on Save Your Breath, mixing electric guitar and organ with four clarinets.
Belgian pianist Nathalie Loriers recorded Nympheas in 1991 with Kurt van Herck, Philippe Aerts and Mimi Verderame, later forming a trio with Postma and Thys.
Saxophonist and flutist Nathan Davis recorded Happy Girl in 1965 with Woody Shaw, Larry Young, Jimmy Woode and Billy Brooks; he composed The Flute in the Blues.
American jazz musician (1937-2003); Recorded on: Adam's Apple; Instruments: guitar; Citizenship: United States.
Japanese trumpeter Natsuki Tamura recorded the freely improvised duo 'How Many?' with pianist Satoko Fujii and played in her big-band album 'South Wind' (1997).
New Orleans trumpeter Natty Dominique recorded with Jelly Roll Morton in 1923 and frequently worked with clarinetist Johnny Dodds, recording with him into 1940.
Keyboardist and arranger Neal Creque played in Pucho and the Latin Soul Brothers, whose Prestige records combined Latin boogaloo, jazz and funk.
Rush drummer and lyricist Neil Peart joined the group in 1974. He debuted on Fly By Night in 1975 and helped shape the 1981 album Moving Pictures.
Canadian jazz bassist Neil Swainson worked with trumpeter Woody Shaw and pianist George Shearing. His own 49th Parallel featured Shaw and Joe Henderson.
Canadian musician (1933-2008); Recorded on: CB Blues; Member of Nelson Symonds Quartet; Instruments: guitar; Citizenship: Canada.
Brazilian guitarist (born 1977) blends classical technique and jazz; played with Pat Metheny and Michel Petrucciani, and recorded for Label Bleu with Magic Malik in 2003.
American musician (1917-1973); Recorded on: Black Butterfly; Instruments: trumpet; Born in Montgomery; Citizenship: United States.
Baritone saxophonist Nick Brignola led the quartet recording This Is It!, switching among saxello, alto, baritone, flute and bass on the session.
Welsh jazz trombonist Nick Evans played with Chris McGregor's Brotherhood of Breath in 1971-75 and joined Elton Dean's Ninesense recordings in 1976-77.
Trumpeter Nick Travis recorded with Zoot Sims on the 1956 Riverside album Zoot! and played arrangements by Gerry Mulligan for Elliot Lawrence.
British musician (1954-1998); Recorded on: A Dream of Fair Women; Member of Acoustic Alchemy; Instruments: guitar; Born in Manchester; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Dutch pianist; Recorded on: Along Came Betty; 1936-2001; Instruments: piano; Born in Amsterdam; Citizenship: Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Italian recording artist; singer and jazz musician (1923-2010); Recorded on: Gratis (feat. Nicola Arigliano); Instruments: voice; Born in Squinzano; Citizenship: Italy.
Flutist Nicole Mitchell played on Mark Dresser Seven's Ain't Nothing But a Cyber Coup & You with Marty Ehrlich, Jim Black and an expanded horn-and-strings group.
British violinist Nigel Kennedy records classical concertos and jazz projects; his Kennedy Meets Gershwin release and SHHH! album show his improvising interests.
Tenor saxophonist Nikele Moyake helped form Cape Town's multiracial Blue Notes with Chris McGregor, Dudu Pukwana, Mongezi Feza, Johnny Dyani and Louis Moholo-Moholo.
British pianist Nikki Iles wrote and played three pieces for the Secret Quartet's Bloor Street and later composed and arranged Face to Face for NDR Bigband.
German pianist; Recorded on: Cafe Del Bozee; born 1964; Instruments: piano; Citizenship: Germany.
Norwegian guitarist and vocalist Nils-Olav Johansen joined Cecilie Grundt Quintet at Dokkhuset in March 2019 on guitar, banjo and voice.
Pianist and vocalist who drew on classical training, blues, jazz, gospel and protest song to build an expressive, genre-defying repertoire.
Free-jazz alto saxophonist Noah Howard led 'The Black Ark' (1969), a fiery ensemble with Arthur Doyle, Muhammad Ali and bassist Sirone.
Singer-bandleader Noble Sissle collaborated with Eubie Blake on the 1921 Broadway musical Shuffle Along and later led an orchestra that featured Lena Horne.
Nigerian-Jamaican jazz violinist, composer and choral conductor; Recorded on: A Flower Is a Lovesome Thing; 1929-2002; Born in Lagos.
Norwegian singer Nora Brockstedt recorded Tango for to for RCA in 1957 with Egil Monn-Iversen's orchestra and later released a Swedish-language repertoire.
Pianist and singer Norah Jones released the Blue Note debut Come Away With Me in February 2002; Arif Mardin produced the final original album.
German composer, music educator and singer; Recorded on: A Night in Tunesia; born 1954; Instruments: guitar, voice; Born in Essen; Citizenship: Germany.
German jazz guitarist Norbert Scholly worked with the WDR Big Band and began teaching jazz guitar at Mainz University in 1997.
American musician; Recorded on: Big "T" Blues; 1911-1996; Instruments: piano; Born in Vernon; Citizenship: United States.
British jazz vocalist Norma Winstone recorded Descansado in March 2017 with Klaus Gesing, Glauco Venier and guests Norbakken and Brunello.
American jazz organist, songwriter (1940-2011); Recorded on: Ain't Shit Happening - Music: Brother Soul, Part 2; Born in Louisville; Citizenship: United States.
Tenor saxophonist Ohad Talmor co-led three projects with Lee Konitz. His Back to the Land group explores newly discovered Ornette Coleman material.
Turkish percussionist Okay Temiz played on Don Cherry's Dona Nostra, recorded in Oslo in March 1993 with Bobo Stenson and Lennart Aberg.
German pianist and university teacher; Recorded on: A Time for Love; Member of Olaf Polziehn Trio; born 1970; Instruments: piano; Born in Ludwigsburg; Citizenship: Germany.
Russian-born Norwegian jazz pianist Olga Konkova recorded the piano-guitar duo December Songs with Jens Thoresen, originally issued in 2017.
German pianist and vocalist Olivia Trummer recorded Fly Now in New York and Berlin in 2013 with bassist Matt Penman and guest Kurt Rosenwinkel.
Israeli bassist Omer Avital formed Qantar in 2016 and released its self-titled quintet album in 2018 with two saxophones, piano and drums.
Clarinetist Omer Simeon recorded with Jelly Roll Morton in 1926 and 1928, then played in Earl Hines's big band and Wilbur DeParis's New Orleans ensemble.
Venezuelan conga player Orlando Poleo performs on Paoli Mejias's 2025 PAPOLEO, adding quitipla and congas to the Latin-jazz arrangement.
Alto saxophonist and composer whose melodically driven free-jazz approach challenged conventional chord progressions and solo roles.
column4: The Shape of Jazz to Come

column3: Jazz pianist Orrin Evans recorded The Magic of Now with Vicente Archer, Bill Stewart and Immanuel Wilkins and led the Captain Black Big Band.
Austrian trumpeter Oscar Klein played in the Tremble Kids revival on MPS and appeared with clarinetist Fatty George and singer Miriam Klein.
Canadian pianist with prodigious technique, a strong swing pulse and rich blues vocabulary; a major trio leader and accompanist.
Steel-pan player Othello Molineaux recorded Opus Pocus on Jaco Pastorius' 1976 solo debut and Liberty City on Word of Mouth, issued in 1981.
Japanese guitarist Otomo Yoshihide led Ground-Zero's 'Consume Red' (1997), building collective noise improvisation around sampled traditional Korean music.
German-born guitarist Ottmar Liebert founded Luna Negra in 1989 and released Nouveau Flamenco after a self-produced Santa Fe recording.
Alto saxophonist Otto Hardwick was an early Duke Ellington colleague, left the orchestra in 1928, returned in 1932 and stayed until 1946.
German pianist Pablo Held expanded his trio into a ten-piece ensemble for GLOW, recording the sessions in March 2010 for a February 2011 release.
British pianist and songwriter Paddy Milner plays blues and New Orleans piano, performing with Tom Jones and the group Jawbone.
Pianist and singer Page Cavanaugh led a swing trio with guitarist Al Viola and bassist Lloyd Pratt, heard on 1947 Armed Forces Radio concerts.
British soul and pop singer Paloma Faith performed in the 2014 BBC Proms with Guy Barker's Jazz Orchestra and the Urban Voices Collective, using orchestral arrangements.
Italian songwriter Paolo Conte first played jazz vibraphone in Asti, wrote Azzurro for Adriano Celentano and later recorded Paris Milonga and Aguaplano.
New Orleans trumpeter and singer Papa Celestin led the Tuxedo Jazz Band, first recorded in 1925 and returned to nationally broadcast performances after World War II.
American musician; Recorded on: A Good Man Nowadays Is Hard to Find; 1910-1977; Instruments: guitar; Born in New Orleans; Citizenship: United States.
Austrian musician, producer and DJ; born 1974; Born in Linz.
Saxophonist Pat LaBarbera toured with Buddy Rich's band before moving to Toronto in 1974. He later worked with Elvin Jones and won a Juno for Deep in a Dream.
Guitarist Pat Martino's leader debut 'El Hombre' (1967) featured Trudy Pitts on organ and Latin percussion, an early soul-jazz guitar statement.
Guitarist and composer recognized for lyrical melodies, spacious ensemble textures and a long-running group with keyboardist Lyle Mays.
Swiss keyboardist Patrick Moraz formed the group Refugee and recorded its 1974 album before joining Yes. His later work included the Moody Blues and the Moraz Alban Project.
German musician; born 1965; Instruments: bass guitar, guitar, bass instrument; Born in Garmisch-Partenkirchen; Citizenship: Germany.
Seattle pianist Patti Bown joined Quincy Jones's 1959 European big-band tour for Free and Easy; she also recorded with Gene Ammons and accompanied Dinah Washington.
Drummer Paul Barbarin wrote New Orleans standard 'Bourbon Street Parade'; his Atlantic recording of January 1955 pairs parade rhythm with jazz improvisation.
Double bassist best known for supple walking lines and melodic solos in Miles Davis's 1950s groups and many hard-bop recordings.
Alto saxophonist Paul Desmond composed 'Take Five' for the Dave Brubeck Quartet's 1959 'Time Out' album, a celebrated experiment in unusual jazz meters.
Saxophonist Paul Dunmall led an octet on Bridging, recorded live at the Jazz em Agosto festival with Keith Tippett, Paul Rutherford and other improvisers.
Austrian composer and jazz musician (1943-2020); Instruments: saxophone; Born in Harmannsdorf.
New Orleans pianist and bandleader Paul Gayten recorded the 1947 De Luxe hit True, led Annie Laurie's band and produced later Chess-associated R&B singles.
South African jazz pianist; Recorded on: Chef's Groove; born 1961; Instruments: piano; Born in Cape Town.
Los Angeles guitarist Paul Jackson Jr. recorded in R&B sessions for artists including the Temptations and Luther Vandross before launching a solo career on Atlantic.
Percussionist Paul Lytton recorded Some Other Season with violinist Philipp Wachsmann in Winterthur in October 1997, and ECM issued the duo in 1999.
Oboist and reed player Paul McCandless explored global sounds in Oregon. The quartet's 1983 ECM album paired him with Ralph Towner, Collin Walcott and Glen Moore.
Trombonist Paul Rutherford joined Paul Dunmall's Bridging octet with Keith Tippett, Gethin Liddington and Tony Levin for a live Jazz em Agosto recording.
Jazz pianist Paul Smith accompanied Karrin Allyson on multiple Concord albums including Daydream and Sweet Home Cookin' and worked at Montreux.
American big band singer (1919-1992); Recorded on: Chattanooga Choo Choo; Member of Al Donahue and His Orchestra; Instruments: voice; Born in Grove City; Citizenship: United States
German trumpeter and composer Peer Baierlein leads the South Quartet and writes scores for theater, chamber groups and electroacoustic duo Dark Fader.
Jazz saxophonist Peggy Gilbert formed all-women bands in the 1930s and later led the Dixie Belles, which toured US jazz events from 1974 to 1996.
Jazz vocalist and songwriter Peggy Lee recorded 'Why Don't You Do Right?' (1942) with Benny Goodman's orchestra; she also wrote and produced her own songs.
American jazz pianist Peggy Stern combines improvised jazz with Latin grooves and played in San Francisco salsa bands.
German jazz bassist Pepe Berns (born 1966) played the 1991 Malta Jazzfest and studied with Charlie Haden; performed in New York with Eliot Zigmund and Ben Monder.
Baritone saxophonist Pepper Adams worked with Kenny Burrell and Paul Chambers in 1955, moved to New York in 1956 and began extensive recording with Donald Byrd in 1958.
Swedish free-jazz pianist Per Henrik Wallin recorded his final solo album Velodromer across two sessions in 2004 and 2005.
Norwegian bassist Per Zanussi led the three-saxophone quintet Zanussi Five, whose self-titled debut appeared in February 2005.
Bassist Percy Heath joined Dizzy Gillespie in 1950 and became a founding member of the Modern Jazz Quartet in 1952 with John Lewis and Milt Jackson.
Bassist Percy Jones joined Shankar and Caroline on The Epidemics, a 1985 studio session featuring 10-string double violin and electronic textures.
Crooner Perry Como recorded for RCA Victor after signing in 1943. He scored a 1945 hit with 'Til the End of Time and won a Grammy for Catch a Falling Star.
Jazz tubist Pete Briggs played with Louis Armstrong's Hot Seven on the 1927 recordings Potato Head Blues and Keyhole Blues, supporting its early rhythm section.
Lead trumpeter Pete Candoli played in the Woody Herman and Stan Kenton big bands and worked in Los Angeles television and recording studios. He also led bands with brother Conte.
West Coast pianist Pete Jolly joined Shorty Rogers's quintet in 1954 and recorded 'Jolly Jumps In' for RCA in 1955 with Shelly Manne and Curtis Counce.
Drummer Pete La Roca led 'Basra' (Blue Note, 1965) with Joe Henderson, Steve Kuhn and Steve Swallow, exploring modal colors inside hard bop.
Vibraphonist Peter Appleyard led the 1990 Concord album Barbados Heat and the 1991 follow-up Barbados Cool with Bucky Pizzarelli and Butch Miles.
Dutch pianist Peter Beets recorded New York Trio - Page Two in Brooklyn on Dec. 16, 2002 with bassist Larry Grenadier and drummer Willie Jones III; released in 2003.
German writer (1957-2003); jazz musician; Recorded on: Brot & Honig; Member of TonArt Ensemble; Born in Hamburg; Citizenship: Germany.
German composer, pianist, keyboardist, organist and author; Recorded on: Der Wegweiser; born 1960; Instruments: piano, organ; Born in Altensteig; Citizenship: Germany.
British smooth-jazz guitarist Peter White released Caravan of Dreams in 1996 after work with Al Stewart and toured with Guitars and Saxes.
Austrian producer and songwriter; jazz musician; Recorded on: A Change in My Life; Member of Gipsy Love; born 1952; Instruments: piano; Born in Vienna.
Tenor saxophonist associated with spiritual jazz; combined fierce overblowing, long modal vamps and searching, vocal-like phrases.
Trumpeter Phil Cohran worked with Sun Ra in Chicago and helped found the AACM in 1965. His Artistic Heritage Ensemble and Frankiphone pursued African-rooted sounds.
Drummer Phil Collins joined jazz-fusion group Brand X in 1975, playing alongside John Goodsall, Percy Jones and Robin Lumley on 1976 album 'Unorthodox Behaviour'.
Drummer, bandleader and singer Phil Harris led radio orchestras and played on The Jack Benny Show from 1936, later voicing Baloo in Disney's Jungle Book.
Belgian guitarist Philip Catherine joined Jean-Luc Ponty's quintet in 1971 and released 'September Man' in 1974, crossing swing and fusion.
Swiss jazz guitarist Philipp Schaufelberger played Kenny Wheeler's Banff Jazz Orchestra and toured with Harald Haerter's quartet, including sets with Dewey Redman.
Belgian bassist Philippe Aerts led the quartet recording Back to the Old World in 2002 with Bert Joris, John Ruocco and drummer Tony Levin.
French electric guitarist Philippe Deschepper recorded MMXXIV AD in Zurich in May 2024 with fellow improvising guitarist Noel Akchote.
Swiss jazz guitarist Pierre Cavalli led popular-music orchestras and recorded guitar with violinist Stephane Grappelli.
French bassist Pierre Michelot played on Miles Davis's improvised 'Ascenseur pour l'echafaud' film score (Paris, December 1957) with Kenny Clarke.
French jazz-rock drummer Pierre Moerlen led a later Gong lineup that featured vibraphone and marimba in its fusion sound.
Dutch pianist Pim Jacobs recorded 1956 trio sides with bassist Ruud Jacobs and drummer Wessel Ilcken and led 1958 Fontana dates with drummer Cees See.
Italian conductor, arranger, bassist, composer and record producer (1943-2026); Recorded on: 20 Years After; Instruments: bass guitar, Rhodes piano; Born in Milan.
Bassist Pops Foster appears on Smithsonian Folkways Town Hall sides with Sidney Bechet and James P. Johnson. Tracks include China Boy, Dear Old Southland and Maple Leaf Rag.
Chicago trombonist Preston Jackson recorded Richard M. Jones' traditional jazz with Darnell Howard and Baby Dodds and later played with Lil Hardin Armstrong.
Italian film director, producer, and screenwriter; jazz musician; Member of Criminal Jazz Band; born 1938; Instruments: clarinet; Born in Bologna; Citizenship: Italy.
Swedish jazz clarinetist Putte Wickman organized a sextet in 1948 that mixed a Goodman-style lineup with arrangements inspired by modern jazz.
Trumpeter, arranger and producer Quincy Jones played with Dizzy Gillespie and directed his touring band. He later produced Michael Jackson's Thriller.
Jazz multi-reed player Rahsaan Roland Kirk used circular breathing and sometimes played several horns simultaneously; he also performed with Charles Mingus.
Experimental trumpeter Rajesh Mehta developed hybrid trumpets, recorded Orka with Paul Lovens and premiered Reconfigurations at MIT in 2001.
American arranger Ralph Burns wrote jazz charts for Woody Herman's orchestra, including Apple Honey and Early Autumn, before film work.
Oregon co-founder Ralph Towner recorded solo classical-guitar album At First Light in Lugano in February 2022 for ECM release in March 2023.
Montenegrin musician Rambo Amadeus issued Hocemo Gusle in 1989, performed Euro Neuro at Eurovision 2012 and composed 2024 studio work with STO1K.
Chicago pianist Ramsey Lewis (1935-2022) blended gospel and jazz; his trio's hit 'The In Crowd' (1965) was recorded live at Bohemian Caverns in Washington, DC.
Pianist and composer Ran Blake brings film noir, gospel and Third Stream ideas to jazz improvisation. He founded a Third Stream program at New England Conservatory.
Philadelphia trumpeter (born 1945) played with Horace Silver and Art Blakey, co-founded the jazz-rock group Dreams and recorded 'Score' (1968) with brother Michael.
American jazz trumpeter and bandleader; Recorded on: Hora Staccato; 1919-1967; Born in Sanford; Citizenship: United States.
Singer Randy Crawford performed the Crusaders' 1979 Street Life and later recorded All Night Long with Joe Sample and No Regrets.
Bassist Randy Jackson played on Jean-Luc Ponty sessions and Tom Coster's early solo albums before producing Randy Jackson's Music Club Vol. 1.
American free jazz drummer; born 1943; Instruments: drum kit; Born in Chicago; Citizenship: United States.
Trumpeter Ray Anthony led an orchestra filmed in 1947 and recorded Thunderbird and Harlem Nocturne for Capitol, as documented by Library of Congress archives.
Ray Charles crossed jazz, gospel and R&B in his singing and piano work. Genius Loves Company paired him with Norah Jones, B.B. King and Gladys Knight.
Arranger Ray Conniff played trombone with Bunny Berigan and Bob Crosby before creating wordless vocal-orchestral recordings for Columbia in the 1950s.
British musician; Recorded on: 51 Stomp; 1928-2002; Instruments: piano; Born in Birmingham; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Congolese pianist Ray Lema recorded the 2016 two-piano album Riddles with Laurent de Wilde and returned to Kinshasa for a Franco Luambo tribute in 2019.
Trumpeter and violinist Ray Nance joined Duke Ellington after work with Earl Hines and Horace Henderson; he soloed on the original Take the A Train.
American musician (1932-2012); Recorded on: Awe; Instruments: saxophone; Born in Boston; Citizenship: United States.
Bassist Red Mitchell led a West Coast quartet with James Clay, Lorraine Geller and Billy Higgins and played in Red Norvo's guitar-vibes-bass trio.
Trumpeter Red Rodney played in dance bands before joining Charlie Parker's quintet. The label Concord documents his return to jazz in the 1970s and later small-group releases.
Ragtime pianist Reginald R. Robinson recorded The Strongman and Euphonic Sounds for Delmark and won a 2004 MacArthur fellowship for his compositions.
German trumpeter Reiner Winterschladen joined the NDR Big Band in 1995 after work in jazz, rock and funk groups.
Vocalist Renee Olstead sang jazz standards at the Pasadena Jazz Institute in 2003 and recorded with pianist Alan Broadbent on Warner.
Pianist Renee Rosnes recorded as a Blue Note leader from 1990 and became music director of ARTEMIS, whose debut Blue Note album arrived in 2020.
British violinist; born 1952; Instruments: violin, mandolin, fiddle; Born in Birmingham; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Jazz euphonium and tuba player Rich Matteson co-led the Matteson-Phillips Tubajazz Consort and taught improvisation at North Texas and the University of North Florida.
Cameroonian bassist and vocalist Richard Bona folds African melody into jazz and Afropop; his collaborations include Pat Metheny and Herbie Hancock.
American pop musician; Recorded on: All Those Years Ago; Member of Carpenters; born 1946; Instruments: piano, voice; Citizenship: United States.
Smooth-jazz saxophonist Richard Elliot began his solo discography with Trolltown in 1986 and recorded Summer Madness for Heads Up in 2016.
Alto saxophonist Richie Cole popularized fast, playful bebop as 'Alto Madness', toured for four years with vocalist Eddie Jefferson and recorded with Phil Woods.
Tenor and soprano saxophonist Rick Margitza recorded and toured with Miles Davis and McCoy Tyner. He also teaches jazz saxophone and arranging at IMEP in Paris.
Singer-songwriter Rickie Lee Jones released her Warner Bros debut in 1979 with Chuck E's in Love. Her second album Pirates appeared in 1981, followed by later jazz projects.
Italian pianist Rita Marcotulli joined Andy Sheppard and Michel Benita on the trio album Salt Catchers, recorded in Lugano in March 2025.
Dutch jazz singer Rita Reys recorded The Cool Voice of Rita Reys in 1956 with the Wessel Ilcken Combo and Art Blakey Jazz Messengers.
Italian film composer (1926-2014); Notable work: More; Instruments: piano; Born in Pesaro; Citizenship: Italy.
Dutch pianist Rob van Kreeveld played North Sea Jazz concerts with Ronald Douglas in 2003 and Xandra Willis in 2006, and taught Amina Figarova.
Italian jazz singer Roberta Gambarini made Easy to Love and So in Love, performed with Hank Jones, and appeared on Roy Hargrove Big Band's Emergence.
Italian jazz drummer Roberto Gatto debuted with Trio di Roma in 1975 and has led albums and taught jazz drums at Santa Cecilia.
Trombonist Robin Eubanks recorded Dave Holland Quintet's The Razor's Edge in February 1987 with Steve Coleman, Kenny Wheeler and Marvin Smith.
German swing vocalist Roger Cicero formed a jazz quartet, released Maennersachen on Warner in 2006 and sang Germany's Eurovision entry in 2007.
Improviser Roger T. Dean played piano and bass with LYSIS and austraLYSIS and released Dualling with Sandy Evans and Phil Slater in 2024.
Austrian vibraphonist Roland Neffe leads the jazz ensemble Vibes Beyond and Wood & Steel Trio; studied with Gary Burton and teaches jazz vibraphone in Nuremberg.
Bassist and cellist whose elastic time and harmonic imagination shaped Miles Davis's 1960s quintet and thousands of recordings.
Drummer Ronald Shannon Jackson led the Decoding Society on Eye on You, recorded in New York in February 1980 with Billy Bang and Vernon Reid.
Trombonist Roswell Rudd played with the New York Art Quartet and Archie Shepp. He later recorded with Malian kora player Toumani Diabate.
Vibraphonist and composer Roy Ayers moved from Atlantic jazz recordings into Verve and Polydor soul-jazz, including Mystic Voyage and Everybody Loves the Sunshine.
Pianist and film composer Roy Budd scored Fear Is the Key with a jazz orchestra featuring Ronnie Scott, Tubby Hayes and Kenny Baker. It included Car Chase.
Jump-blues bandleader Roy Milton recorded R.M. Blues with His Solid Senders for the Specialty catalog, whose reissues document work from 1947 to 1953.
New Orleans guitarist Roy Montrell helped found AFO Records in 1961, recorded sessions with Fats Domino and issued That Mellow Saxophone.
Sicilian trumpeter Roy Paci joined The Ex and Brass Unbound on Enormous Door in 2013 and recorded with Nigerian singer Chris Obehi.
German guitarist and composer Rue Protzer leads the group 4 at the club and runs the Guitar Nova label, producing jazz and other guitar-based music.
Tenor saxophonist Rusty Bryant began leading Columbus bands in 1951 and returned to recording in 1968 with Groove Holmes before a series of Prestige albums.
Japanese alto saxophonist Sadao Watanabe studied at Berklee, recorded the 1969 album Pastoral and joined Hank Jones, Ron Carter and Tony Williams for Carnaval in 1978.
Algerian composer Safy Boutella co-produced Khaled's Kutche project and released the 1992 fusion album Mejnoun, composing Orient and Nomade.
Alto saxophonist Sahib Shihab recorded with Thelonious Monk, Milt Jackson, Al McKibbon and Art Blakey for Blue Note at WOR Studios on July 23, 1951.
American jazz guitarist (1939-1977); Born in St. Louis; Citizenship: United States.
Bassist Sam Jones composed 'Unit 7' with Cannonball Adderley; his 1960 Riverside album 'The Soul Society' also featured his jazz cello.
New York drummer Sam Ulano published his first drum-method book in 1948, taught through World of Drums and performed with Moondog and Public Image Ltd.
Singer Sammy Davis Jr. recorded What Kind of Fool Am I for Reprise and appeared with Frank Sinatra and Dean Martin on an armed-forces radio disc.
Big-band arranger Sammy Nestico wrote for Count Basie's orchestra, led the Airmen of Note and published hundreds of jazz arrangements for schools.
Tenor saxophonist Sandy Mosse recorded Chicago Scene for Argo in 1956 and a 1981 Chicago quintet session with bass trumpeter Cy Touff.
Jazz singer Sara Gazarek issued Thirsty Ghost in 2019 with pianist Stu Mindeman and drummer Christian Euman; it earned a Grammy nomination.
Singer renowned for an operatic vocal range, sophisticated harmony and flexible phrasing across ballads and up-tempo jazz.
Singer Sathima Bea Benjamin recorded African Songbird in 1976 with Abdullah Ibrahim and bassist Louis Spears. Her later Ekapa label supported South African jazz.
Pianist/composer Satoko Fujii led the 1997 'South Wind' big band, using intricate written passages and fiery free improvisation with trumpeter Natsuki Tamura.
American musician (1942-1999); Instruments: piano, voice; Born in El Monte; Citizenship: United States.
Saxophonist Scheila Gonzalez toured with Zappa Plays Zappa, received a 2009 ensemble Grammy for Peaches en Regalia and joined Colin Hay's band.
Ragtime pianist/composer (c.1868-1917), a jazz precursor. Published 'Maple Leaf Rag' (1899) in Sedalia and wrote 'The Entertainer' and the opera 'Treemonisha'.
Italian trombonist Sebi Tramontana played in the December 1997 Italian Instabile Orchestra festival set and co-led Canzone a Due.
French songwriter Serge Gainsbourg began recording for Philips in 1958 with arranger Alain Goraguer. His early Le Poinconneur des Lilas drew on jazz and chanson.
Soviet improviser Sergey Kuryokhin organized Pop Mekhanika performances and recorded free-jazz experiments with visiting collaborators.
Philadelphia saxophonist Shafi Hadi, formerly Curtis Porter, played alto and tenor on Charles Mingus albums The Clown and New Tijuana Moods in the late 1950s.
Japanese saxophonist Shinji Takeda issued his debut single Blow up in 1995, recorded Breath of Life and led a Blue Note Tokyo concert in July 2022.
Singer-pianist Shirley Horn recorded Embers and Ashes in 1960, opened for Miles Davis at the Village Vanguard and reunited with him on You Won't Forget Me in 1990.
Japanese trumpeter Shunzo Ohno moved to New York after working with Art Blakey, played on Machito's acclaimed big-band album and led Bubbles.
Trombonist Si Zentner joined Les Brown in 1940, formed a Liberty Records swing orchestra in 1959 and won a Grammy for Up a Lazy River.
South African singer Sibongile Khumalo released Ancient Evenings in 1996 and Live at the Market Theatre in 1998, blending African song and jazz.
New Orleans clarinetist and soprano saxophonist (1897-1959), known for expressive vibrato. Hear 'Summertime'; toured Europe with Will Marion Cook and later lived in France.
Norwegian vocalist Silje Nergaard joined Espen Berg Trio on the Paul Simon song I'd Do It For Your Love, released in March 2022.
Swedish jazz bassist Simon Brehm led a Bal Palais dance band, started the Karusell label in 1952 and recruited singer Lill-Babs for a 1954 tour.
Norwegian singer Simone Eriksrud co-founded D'Sound in 1993, singing on its jazz-soul debut Spice of Life and later returning to the group.
Bassist Sirone joined Charles Gayle and Gerald Cleaver for the studio trio release Shout, pairing exploratory tenor saxophone with agile acoustic rhythm.
Brazilian accordionist Sivuca worked with Miriam Makeba as guitarist and bandleader and recorded a 1984 accordion duo with Chiquinho do Acordeom.
Guitarist Skeeter Best recorded with Etta Jones on the 1960 Prestige album Don't Go to Strangers and in Mercer Ellington's 1958 orchestra.
Pianist-conductor Skitch Henderson founded the New York Pops in 1983 and conducted a Carnegie Hall program featuring My Funny Valentine.
Trumpeter Snooky Young played lead with Jimmie Lunceford in 1939-42, helped found the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra in 1966 and joined The Tonight Show band.
Clarinetist Sol Yaged played a 1954 Jack Teagarden session and appeared at New York's Pied Piper in 1947 with Rex Stewart and Doc Pomus.
Norwegian vocalist Solveig Slettahjell contributed to Jon Balke's Batagraf album Statements, made during 2003-04 and released by ECM in 2005.
American musician and music educator; Recorded on: "Where Have You Been Billy Boy"; born 1936; Instruments: drum kit; Born in Cincinnati; Citizenship: United States.
Tenor saxophonist celebrated for thematic improvisation, rhythmic wit and unaccompanied cadenzas. Saxophone Colossus showcases his musical storytelling.
Swiss songwriter Sophie Hunger released albums including Monday's Ghost and Molecules and records for the Two Gentlemen label.
Russian-born Canadian jazz singer Sophie Milman combines classic standards with contemporary jazz arrangements and international influences.
Drummer Specs Powell became the first Black staff musician at a US national network when CBS hired him in 1943. He played in the Ed Sullivan orchestra from 1947 to 1972.
British musician; born 1975; Instruments: guitar; Born in Chelmsford; Citizenship: United Kingdom.
Tenor saxophonist admired for a smooth lyrical sound, from cool jazz to Brazilian bossa nova collaborations with Joao Gilberto.
Pianist and bandleader Stan Kenton recorded 'Artistry in Rhythm' for Capitol in November 1943; his orchestra later explored modern jazz with arranger Pete Rugolo.
Bebop drummer Stan Levey worked with Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker in 1945, then joined Stan Kenton orchestra in 1952.
British pianist Stan Tracey led the 1965 Under Milk Wood quartet with Bobby Wellins, Jeff Clyne and drummer Jackie Dougan after backing guests at Ronnie Scott's.
Pianist Stanley Cowell recorded Illusion Suite with Stanley Clarke and Jimmy Hopps in New York in November 1972; its original release followed in 1973.
German saxophonist Steffen Weber co-founded L14,16, played in the SWR Big Band from 2008 to 2012 and joined the Frankfurt Radio Big Band in 2012.
Multi-instrumentalist Stephan Micus studies instruments worldwide and overdubs them in solo compositions. His 2024 album To the Rising Moon featured Colombian tiples.
Cornetist Sterling Bose played in Joe Haymes's big band and performed with the Original Crescent City Jazzers before later swing-orchestra work.
Improviser Steve Beresford supplied electronics to Simon H. Fell's large-ensemble work Positions & Descriptions alongside Tim Berne and Rhodri Davies.
jazz musician best known for his work on string bass (1890-1965); Recorded on: "Gimme" a Little Kiss, Will "Ya"? Huh?; Instruments: double bass; Born in New Orleans.
English drummer Steve Harris founded the improvising group Zaum, recorded a 2007 Brighton concert and played a late duet with saxophonist Jan Kopinski.
Pianist Steve Kuhn played in John Coltrane's quartet in 1960; his ECM trio album 'Wisteria' (2012) united Steve Swallow and Joey Baron.
Guitarist Steve Lukather co-founded Toto and played on Michael Jackson's Thriller. His solo album Lukather features guest musicians including Eddie Van Halen and Jan Hammer.
Vibraphonist Steve Nelson recorded Dave Holland Quintet's Points of View in September 1997, alternating vibes and marimba in the new band.
Bassist Steve Rodby recorded First Circle with the Pat Metheny Group at New York's Power Station in February 1984 alongside Lyle Mays.
Trombonist Steve Turre recorded Avant Pop with Lester Bowie's Brass Fantasy at Tonstudio Bauer in March 1986 and contributed two compositions.
British saxophonist Steve Williamson began on clarinet, took up saxophone at sixteen and drew early inspiration from jazz-funk records.
Serbian trumpeter Stjepko Gut played in the Markovic-Gut Sextet, taught jazz in Graz from 1985 and appeared at the 1999 Trumpet Summit.
Bulgarian drummer Stoyan Yankulov spent seven years in the national radio big band and combined jazz drumming with Bulgarian folk percussion.
Bassist Stuart Zender performed and co-wrote Jamiroquai's 1996 tracks Virtual Insanity and Travelling Without Moving, before the 2016 remasters.
Percussionist Sue Evans recorded Steve Kuhn's Trance in November 1974 and played on George Benson's CTI album Good King Bad in 1975.
Pianist, composer and bandleader who united large-ensemble jazz, electronic textures and Afrofuturist performance art in his Arkestra.
Free-jazz drummer Sunny Murray led a January 1966 New York ESP-Disk session with Alan Silva, Jacques Coursil and Byard Lancaster.
Swiss-Dutch jazz vocalist Susanne Abbuehl recorded April for ECM in 2000 and later made Compass with pianist Wolfert Brederode and drummer Lucas Niggli.
German-born Amsterdam saxophonist Susanne Alt recorded Royalty for Real in New York with James Hurt, Gerald Cannon and Willie Jones III.
American actress (1929-2002); jazz musician; Born in Detroit; Citizenship: United States.
Norwegian pianist and visual artist Svein Finnerud formed a free-jazz trio in 1967 and issued Plastic Sun in 1970.
Norwegian jazz pianist Svein Olav Herstad led piano trios and wrote Suite for Simmons for the 2005 Sildajazz festival.
French guitarist Sylvain Luc released Piaia in 1993 and later recorded duo albums with Louis Winsberg and Bireli Lagrene.
Bassist Tarus Mateen worked in Betty Carter's band and formed Jason Moran's Bandwagon trio with drummer Nasheet Waits on Facing Left and Ten.
Trumpeter Ted Curson recorded Tears for Dolphy in Paris on August 1 1964 with Bill Barron, Herb Bushler and drummer Dick Berk.
British trombonist and bandleader Ted Heath led a swing orchestra associated with London Palladium performances and films from 1946 through 1960.
American jazz singer Teddi King recorded intimate Storyville sessions in 1954 and 1955 with swing musicians including Ruby Braff and Bob Brookmeyer.
American vibraphonist Teddy Charles explored bebop and Third Stream jazz, leading Prestige sessions and working with Charles Mingus.
Los Angeles tenor saxophonist Teddy Edwards worked with Howard McGhee and recorded the Contemporary albums Teddy's Ready and Together Again! in the 1960s.
Bandleader Teddy Hill led a successful 1930s swing orchestra and later managed Harlem's Minton's Playhouse, where after-hours jam sessions fostered early bebop.
Bassist Teddy Smith played with Clifford Jordan and Cedar Walton on Bearcat and with Kenny Dorham and Jackie McLean on the 1962 Matador session.
Swiss saxophonist Teddy Stauffer led the Original Teddies swing orchestra in Berlin and recorded Moeni Stomp for Elite in 1940.
Producer and tenor saxophonist Teo Macero shaped Miles Davis's Columbia albums through studio editing and recorded the Third Stream album Teo.
Trumpeter Terence Blanchard recorded the Herbie Hancock-produced Flow in 2005 and led Magnetic in 2013, featuring Ron Carter and Lionel Loueke.
Chicago vocalist-guitarist Terry Callier recorded The New Folk Sound in 1965 and made the Cadet albums Occasional Rain and What Color Is Love in 1972.
Trumpeter Terumasa Hino recorded 'Taro's Mood' in June 1973 with pianist Mikio Masuda, bassist Yoshio Ikeda and drummer Motohiko Hino.
Trumpeter and arranger Thad Jones co-founded the Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra in 1966; his modern big-band charts were heard on Mondays at the Village Vanguard.
Horace Silver's hard-bop quintet recorded '6 Pieces of Silver' (1956) for Blue Note; 'Senor Blues' featured Donald Byrd, Hank Mobley, Doug Watkins and Louis Hayes.
Pianist Oscar Peterson's trio with Herb Ellis on guitar and Ray Brown on bass recorded live at the Stratford Shakespearean Festival in 1956; hear 'Noreen's Nocturne'.
American actress and musician (1922-1997); Recorded on: Alexander's Ragtime Band; Instruments: voice; Born in Brooklyn; Citizenship: United States.
Pianist and composer known for spare, angular melodies, distinctive dissonance and unexpected silence. Wrote Round Midnight, Blue Monk and Straight, No Chaser.
British saxophonist and flautist Theo Travis leads Double Talk and has performed with Soft Machine and Robert Fripp.
Bulgarian kaval virtuoso Theodosii Spassov integrates folk flute, jazz and classical music in original compositions and collaborations.
Pianist Thomas A. Dorsey recorded blues as Georgia Tom, directed Pilgrim Baptist Church's choir and narrated his life on 1973's Precious Lord.
German actor (1942-2023); jazz musician; Recorded on: Bibelworte des Allmachtigen; Member of Abbi Hubner's Low Down Wizards; Instruments: drum kit; Born in Berlin.
Austrian trumpeter Thomas Gansch co-founded Mnozil Brass and played in Vienna Art Orchestra (1998-2006); also leads jazz quintets and teaches trumpet in Vienna.
German saxophonist Thomas Klemm recorded ChoralConcert with Karl Scharnweber and Wolfgang Schmiedt in 1990 and joined Wroblewsky and Donner in 1991.
Austrian drummer Thomas Lang studied at the Vienna Conservatory, worked with the Vienna Art Orchestra and released the solo album Mediator.
Classical baritone Thomas Quasthoff recorded jazz standards on Nice 'n' Easy with the NDR Big Band in 2018, joined by Frank Chastenier and Dieter Ilg.
Norwegian guitarist Thomas T Dahl joined Mats Eilertsen's septet for Rubicon, recorded at Rainbow Studio in Oslo in May 2015.
Danish singer; born 1968; Instruments: voice; Born in Copenhagen; Citizenship: Kingdom of Denmark.
Armenian jazz pianist Tigran Hamasyan's 'Mockroot' (2015) mixes Armenian folk songs, intricate jazz rhythms, rock, voice and electronic textures.
Alto saxophonist Tim Berne recorded 'Snakeoil' for ECM in 2011; the 2012 quartet album features Oscar Noriega, Matt Mitchell and Ches Smith in chamber-like free jazz.
British reed player Tim Garland released Songs to the North Sky in 2014, combining saxophones and bass clarinet with strings, piano and percussion.
Dutch violinist Tim Kliphuis blends gypsy jazz, folk and classical music. His trio includes guitarist Nigel Clark and bassist Roy Percy, alongside orchestral projects.
Australian singer Tina Arena records pop ballads in English and French, with releases including Don't Ask and the later Love Saves.
Tenor saxophonist Tina Brooks recorded Minor Move in 1958 with Lee Morgan, Sonny Clark, Doug Watkins and Art Blakey; the hard-bop album was unreleased until 1980.
British jazz singer Tina May studied classical singing at Cardiff and was awarded a jazz education honor in 2003.
Trumpeter Tom Browne joined the emerging GRP Records roster and mixed jazz improvisation with funk on hits such as Funkin' for Jamaica and Thighs High.
German singer Tom Gaebel began leading his own big band in Cologne in 2005. His debut Introducing: Myself mixes swing singing and easy-listening arrangements.
Multi-brass session musician Tom Malone played tuba on Willie Colon and Ruben Blades's Metiendo mano! and joined Ron Carter's horn section on Parade.
Drummer-composer Tom Skinner released Voices of Bishara in November 2022 with Nubya Garcia, Shabaka Hutchings, Tom Herbert and Kareem Dayes.
Arranger Tom Talbert produced Patty McGovern's 1956 Atlantic album Wednesday's Child and composed The Moonshower, recorded by Kai Winding in 1951.
Swing trombonist Tommy Dorsey's orchestra paired Sy Oliver's hot arrangements with the 1940 debut of vocalist Frank Sinatra; hear 'Opus One'.
Australian guitarist Tommy Emmanuel developed a percussive fingerstyle approach and recorded with Chet Atkins while exploring jazz, pop and roots music.
Jamaican tenor saxophonist and flutist Tommy McCook helped shape ska with the Skatalites after studying jazz. His recording career also included the Supersonics.
Hard-bop trumpeter Tommy Turrentine led a Time Records session in New York on January 19, 1960 with Stanley Turrentine, Horace Parlan and Max Roach.
jazz musician from America; born 1934; Instruments: double bass; Citizenship: United States.
American singer Tony Bennett performed jazz standards with small groups and made a series of independent Improv recordings in the 1970s.
Australian drummer Tony Buck co-founded improvised-music trio The Necks with Chris Abrahams and Lloyd Swanton in 1986; its hypnotic music unfolds slowly.
Houston-born saxophonist and flutist Tony Campise joined Stan Kenton's orchestra in the 1970s and later settled in Austin, where he worked in jazz education.
Spanish actor, director, and comedian (1922-2012); jazz musician; Born in Madrid; Citizenship: Spain.
Bassist Tony Levin's jazz credits include Buddy Rich, Gary Burton and Steps Ahead; his Chapman Stick work also shaped progressive jazz-rock projects.
British drummer Tony Oxley worked as house drummer at Ronnie Scott's and recorded the exploratory album Baptized Traveller in 1969.
Drummer Tony Sbarbaro played in the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, appearing on the Victor recording Dixieland Jass Band One-Step made in New York in 1917.
Drummer whose explosive polyrhythms reshaped Miles Davis's 1960s quintet and helped drive early electric fusion.
Brazilian guitarist and singer Toquinho (born 1946) partnered with poet Vinicius de Moraes on songs such as 'Tarde em Itapoa'; his solo repertoire includes 'Aquarela'.
German guitarist and singer Torsten Goods draws on jazz, blues, soul and pop. After studying in New York, he released Irish Heart on ACT in 2006.
Norwegian tenor saxophonist Totti Bergh performed with Al Cohn on Tenor Gladness and with Plas Johnson on On the Trail!, both for Gemini.
Lebanese-born saxophonist Toufic Farroukh composes jazz with Middle Eastern timbres and recorded Ali on Broadway and Drab Zeen.
Trombonist Troy Andrews led Trombone Shorty and Orleans Avenue, debuting on Blue Note in 2017 with Chris Seefried-produced Parking Lot Symphony.
Norwegian saxophonist and composer Trygve Seim recorded Different Rivers and Helsinki Songs for ECM, as well as the duo album Our Time with Frode Haltli.
New Orleans pianist Tuts Washington worked with guitarist Smiley Lewis on Imperial sides such as Tee-Nah-Nah. His solo piano album New Orleans Piano Professor came out in 1983.
Philadelphia bassist Tyrone Brown succeeded Alphonso Johnson in Catalyst and played in Pat Martino's Prestige-era bands for East! and Desperado.
German bassist Uli Trepte played in the Irene Schweizer Trio and Guru Guru, later led Spacebox and compiled his career album Portrait for Sireena.
Japanese jazz/hip-hop producer Uyama Hiroto collaborated with Nujabes and released 'A Son of the Sun' (2008), later establishing roph recordings and exploring free jazz.
Trumpeter-vocalist Valaida Snow appeared in the 1924 revue The Chocolate Dandies and led Chicago's Sunset Cafe bill in 1928 while touring widely as a performer.
Greek pianist Vassilis Tsabropoulos combines piano improvisation with Byzantine-inspired composition in chamber recordings for ECM.
Jazz singer Velma Middleton joined Louis Armstrong's band in 1942. She performed comic duets and sang on Armstrong albums Plays W.C. Handy and Satch Plays Fats.
American jazz band leader (1902-1966); Instruments: violin; Citizenship: United States.
Hungarian singer Veronika Harcsa recorded Lampafeny in Budapest in January 2011 with pianist Attila Blaho and guitarist Balint Gyemant.
American musician (1896-1951); Recorded on: 'Tain't Cold; Member of Four Instrumental Stars; Instruments: piano; Born in Chicago; Citizenship: United States.
Acoustic guitarist Vicki Genfan uses a slap-tap technique and appeared on the La Guitara compilation. She won Guitar Player magazine's Guitar Superstar competition.
American musician (1950-2025); Instruments: guitar, bass guitar; Born in Fresno; Citizenship: United States.
New Orleans clarinetist and saxophonist Victor Goines performed with the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and Wynton Marsalis Septet. He also led jazz studies at Northwestern.
Filipino American jazz pianist Victor Noriega released Stone's Throw and Alay, and composed Generations, Directions for Oakland East Bay Symphony.
Chicago jazz bassist Victor Sproles recorded with Sun Ra on Sound of Joy and backed Eddie Davis and Johnny Griffin on Battle Stations.
Spanish actress; jazz musician; Recorded on: Luna Negra (edit radio); Member of Les Grosses Tetes; born 1959; Instruments: voice; Born in Madrid; Citizenship: Spain.
Actor and improvisational musician Viggo Mortensen recorded with guitarist Buckethead; their experimental album 'One Less Thing to Worry About' appeared in 1997.
French horn player Vincent Chancey joined Lester Bowie's nine-piece Brass Fantasy for Avant Pop, recorded at Tonstudio Bauer in March 1986.
German chef, author, editor, publisher of culinary literature and famous TV chef; jazz musician; Recorded on: Beautiful Love; born 1949; Born in Giessen; Citizenship: Germany.
Double bassist Vinnie Burke recorded 1956 ABC-Paramount All-Stars sessions and a 1957 String Jazz Quartet album with Dick Wetmore and Calo Scott.
Drummer Vinnie Colaiuta performed on John McLaughlin's Five Peace Band Live and contributed to The Wind Cries Mary with Sting and McLaughlin, according to Grammy credits.
Baritone saxophonist Virgil Gonsalves recorded a 1954 Nocturne sextet with Lou Levy and a 1955 Liberty sextet with Dan Patiris and Clyde Pound.
Italian singer and pianist Virgilio Savona performed with Quartetto Cetra in a 1964 RAI broadcast and co-wrote the 1966 television program Cetra 66.
German guitarist Volker Kriegel features on ECM's Atmospheric Conditions Permitting, a Hessischer Rundfunk jazz-ensemble collection spanning 1967 to 1993.
Pianist Wade Legge joined Dizzy Gillespie after being heard as a bassist by Milt Jackson; he later recorded with Sonny Rollins and Charles Mingus.
Trumpeter Wallace Roney played with Art Blakey and Tony Williams and appeared alongside Miles Davis at Montreux in 1991 for music arranged by Gil Evans.
Saxophonist Walt Weiskopf played in Buddy Rich Big Band in 1981 and issued the leader album Simplicity for Criss Cross in 1993.
Chicago bandmaster Walter Dyett taught Nat King Cole, Johnny Griffin and Dinah Washington while directing the music program at DuSable High School.
German light, sound and media artist (1937-2016); jazz musician; Born in Mannweiler; Citizenship: Germany.
Composer and arranger Walter Murphy adapted classical themes for disco, earning a Grammy nomination for A Fifth of Beethoven, and worked on Family Guy Live in Vegas.
Tenor saxophonist Walter Smith III released Blue Note debut return to casual in 2023 with Taylor Eigsti, Matt Stevens and Kendrick Scott.
Percussionist Warren Smith recorded on Enrico Rava's Quotation Marks, an adventurous album with Jeanne Lee, John Abercrombie and Jack DeJohnette.
American electric bassist Wayman Tisdale pursued smooth jazz recording alongside professional basketball, releasing several leader albums.
Jazz Crusaders trombonist Wayne Henderson wrote Keep That Same Old Feeling and produced 1970s soul-funk projects for Side Effect and Pleasure.
American guitarist Wayne Krantz leads electric improvising groups and recorded with drummers Zach Danziger and Keith Carlock.
Saxophonist and composer whose enigmatic melodies shaped the Jazz Messengers, Miles Davis's quintet and Weather Report.
German jazz guitarist Werner Neumann teaches at Leipzig and has performed with Richie Beirach and Napoleon Murphy Brock.
Guitarist whose warm thumb-picked tone, octave melodies and chord solos became hallmarks of modern jazz guitar.
column4: The Incredible Jazz Guitar of Wes Montgomery

column3: Drummer Whit Dickey recorded the cornet-drums duo Fierce Silence with Kirk Knuffke in Brooklyn on October 14, 2015.
Bassist Wilbur Ware anchored Thelonious Monk's 1957 groups with John Coltrane and played Sonny Rollins's 'A Night at the Village Vanguard' sessions.
Trumpeter Frankie Newton backed Billie Holiday's April 1939 Commodore recordings of 'Strange Fruit' and 'Fine and Mellow' in his Cafe Society Orchestra.
Wilton Felder appeared on acclaimed recordings with the Crusaders and earned Grammy nominations under his name. These projects moved between R&B and instrumental jazz.
Trumpeter Wingy Manone wrote and arranged scores and published the autobiography Trumpet on the Wing. He settled in Las Vegas in 1954 and played in hotels while touring.
South African tenor saxophonist Winston Mankunku Ngozi recorded Yakhal' Inkomo in 1968 with Lionel Pillay, Agrippa Magwaza and Early Mabuza.
Guitarist Wolfgang Muthspiel led ECM's 'Rising Grace' (2016) with Ambrose Akinmusire, Brad Mehldau, Larry Grenadier and Brian Blade.
Austrian reed player Wolfgang Puschnig recorded with Red Sun and Korean percussion group SamulNori in Seoul in May 1993 for ECM's White Tiger.
Trombonist Wolter Wierbos played at Jazzfest Berlin in 2016 with Alexander von Schlippenbach's Globe Unity Orchestra for its fiftieth anniversary.
Clarinetist and bandleader Woody Herman's orchestra recorded Jimmy Giuffre's 'Four Brothers' in Hollywood (1947), featuring Stan Getz, Zoot Sims and Serge Chaloff.
Trumpeter Woody Shaw (1944-1989) broadened modern jazz harmony; recorded 'Unity' with Larry Young (1965) and led the album 'Rosewood' (1977).
Dutch jazz-pop singer Wouter Hamel made his North Sea Jazz Festival debut in 2005 and released Hamel, Nobody's Tune and the self-produced Lohengrin.
Bassist Wyatt Ruther led a 1955 Basses Loaded date and joined Toshiko Akiyoshi's quartet in 1956 and Buddy Rich's small group in 1961.
Blues shouter Wynonie Harris recorded Good Rockin' Tonight and Good Morning Judge for King Records. His rhythm-and-blues recordings helped shape early rock-and-roll singing.
Pianist Wynton Kelly recorded fourteen Blue Note trio tracks in 1951, played with Miles Davis from 1959 to 1963 and then formed a trio with Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb.
Trumpeter and educator whose virtuosity, traditional jazz advocacy and leadership at Jazz at Lincoln Center influenced modern jazz institutions.
Jazz pianist Yaron Herman released the Blue Note album 'Everyday' (2015) with drummer Ziv Ravitz, linking solo piano and percussive textures.
Classical violinist Yehudi Menuhin recorded swing standards with jazz violinist Stephane Grappelli, including Jealousy at Abbey Road in 1973.
Composer Yoko Kanno leads the Seatbelts, whose 1998 'Cowboy Bebop' soundtrack mixed big-band jazz, blues and rock; she composed and arranged the theme 'Tank!'.
Ceylon-born jazz singer Yolande Bavan succeeded Annie Ross in the Lambert and Hendricks vocal trio and sang in The Real Ambassadors at Monterey in 1962.
Korean pianist and singer-songwriter Younha debuted in Japan in 2004. Her 2021 album End Theory includes Oort Cloud; Growth Theory followed in 2024.
Ukrainian saxophonist; born 1951; Born in Novokuznetsk; Citizenship: Soviet Union.
Saxophonist and flutist (1920-2013) brought global timbres to jazz; played with Dizzy Gillespie and Cannonball Adderley. Hear 'Eastern Sounds' (1961); toured Europe and Japan.
Jazz violinist Zach Brock played in Snarky Puppy on Culcha Vulcha (2016) and Empire Central (2022), then joined Oberlin faculty in 2026.
Guitarist Zachary Breaux performed with Roy Ayers and released his NYC Records album Laidback in 1994, featuring harmonica guest Toots Thielemans.
American musician (1898-1967); Instruments: banjo; Born in Richmond; Citizenship: United States.
Indian tabla player Zakir Hussain recorded with Shakti and worked across Indian classical, world music and jazz, including ECM albums and the 2023 As We Speak.
Polish violinist Zbigniew Seifert recorded Man of the Light with Joachim Kuhn, Cecil McBee and Billy Hart in 1976; MPS released the album in 1977.
Electric-harp improviser Zeena Parkins formed Phantom Orchard with electronic musician Ikue Mori, recording their self-titled 2004 album.
Trumpeter Ziggy Elman played with Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey, and his own band recorded And the Angels Sing, a hit in 1939.
South African reed player Zim Ngqawana released four Sheer Sound studio albums: Zimology, Ingoma, Zimphonic Suites and Vadzimu.
Austrian jazz violinist Zipflo Weinrich drew on Sinti swing traditions and recorded with international jazz musicians while developing his own sound.
British jazz pianist Zoe Rahman combines classical study with Bengali musical roots. Her work includes Colour of Sound and collaborations with her brother Idris Rahman.
French jazz musician; born 1958; Instruments: piano; Born in Boulogne-Billancourt; Citizenship: France.
New Orleans drummer Zutty Singleton played on Louis Armstrong's 1928 Hot Five 'Knee Drops' and 'West End Blues' era sessions with Earl Hines.
